units.leftText: These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel in the wilderness east of the Jordan — in the Arabah opposite Suph — between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
units.rightText: These are the words which Moses spake unto all Israel beyond the Jordan in the wilderness, in the Arabah over against Suph, between Paran, and Tophel, and Laban, and Hazeroth, and Di-zahab.

units.leftText: It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea by way of Mount Seir.
units.rightText: It is eleven days’ journey from Horeb by the way of mount Seir unto Kadesh-barnea.
leftNotes: 1:2 That is, Mount Sinai, or possibly a mountain in the range containing Mount Sinai; also in verses 6 and 19

units.leftText: In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses proclaimed to the Israelites all that the LORD had commanded him concerning them.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, that Moses spake unto the children of Israel, according unto all that Jehovah had given him in commandment unto them;

units.leftText: This was after he had defeated Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and then at Edrei had defeated Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth.
units.rightText: after he had smitten Sihon the king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, who dwelt in Ashtaroth, at Edrei.

units.leftText: On the east side of the Jordan in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this law, saying:
units.rightText: Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, began Moses to declare this law, saying,
leftNotes: 1:5 Note that Deuteronomy 1:6|DEU 1:6* through Deuteronomy 4:40 may be presented as a continuous section of unbroken speech by Moses. In place of multiple levels of nested quotes, this section has been set apart with a double space.

units.leftText: The LORD our God said to us at Horeb: “You have stayed at this mountain long enough.
units.rightText: Jehovah our God spake unto us in Horeb, saying, Ye have dwelt long enough in this mountain:

units.leftText: Resume your journey and go to the hill country of the Amorites; go to all the neighboring peoples in the Arabah, in the hill country, in the foothills, in the Negev, and along the seacoast to the land of the Canaanites and to Lebanon, as far as the great River Euphrates.
units.rightText: turn you, and take your journey, and go to the hill-country of the Amorites, and unto all the places nigh thereunto, in the Arabah, in the hill-country, and in the lowland, and in the South, and by the sea-shore, the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the river Euphrates.
leftNotes: 1:7 Hebrew Shephelah or lowlands; that is, the western foothills of Judea

units.leftText: See, I have placed the land before you. Enter and possess the land that the LORD swore He would give to your fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to their descendants after them.” Moses Appoints Leaders (Exodus 18:13–27|EXO 18:13-27*)
units.rightText: Behold, I have set the land before you: go in and possess the land which Jehovah sware unto your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give unto them and to their seed after them.

units.leftText: At that time I said to you, “I cannot carry the burden for you alone.
units.rightText: And I spake unto you at that time, saying, I am not able to bear you myself alone:

units.leftText: The LORD your God has multiplied you, so that today you are as numerous as the stars in the sky.
units.rightText: Jehovah your God hath multiplied you, and, behold, ye are this day as the stars of heaven for multitude.

units.leftText: May the LORD, the God of your fathers, increase you a thousand times over and bless you as He has promised.
units.rightText: Jehovah, the God of your fathers, make you a thousand times as many as ye are, and bless you, as he hath promised you!

units.leftText: But how can I bear your troubles, burdens, and disputes all by myself?
units.rightText: How can I myself alone bear your cumbrance, and your burden, and your strife?

units.leftText: Choose for yourselves wise, understanding, and respected men from each of your tribes, and I will appoint them as your leaders.”
units.rightText: Take you wise men, and understanding, and known, according to your tribes, and I will make them heads over you.

units.leftText: And you answered me and said, “What you propose to do is good.”
units.rightText: And ye answered me, and said, The thing which thou hast spoken is good for us to do.

units.leftText: So I took the leaders of your tribes, wise and respected men, and appointed them as leaders over you — as commanders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens, and as officers for your tribes.
units.rightText: So I took the heads of your tribes, wise men, and known, and made them heads over you, captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds, and captains of fifties, and captains of tens, and officers, according to your tribes.

units.leftText: At that time I charged your judges: “Hear the disputes between your brothers, and judge fairly between a man and his brother or a foreign resident.
units.rightText: And I charged your judges at that time, saying, Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between a man and his brother, and the sojourner that is with him.

units.leftText: Show no partiality in judging; hear both small and great alike. Do not be intimidated by anyone, for judgment belongs to God. And bring to me any case too difficult for you, and I will hear it.”
units.rightText: Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; ye shall hear the small and the great alike; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s: and the cause that is too hard for you ye shall bring unto me, and I will hear it.

units.leftText: And at that time I commanded you all the things you were to do. Twelve Spies Sent Out (Numbers 13:1–33|NUM 13:1-33*)
units.rightText: And I commanded you at that time all the things which ye should do.

units.leftText: And just as the LORD our God had commanded us, we set out from Horeb and went toward the hill country of the Amorites, through all the vast and terrifying wilderness you have seen. When we reached Kadesh-barnea,
units.rightText: And we journeyed from Horeb, and went through all that great and terrible wilderness which ye saw, by the way to the hill-country of the Amorites, as Jehovah our God commanded us; and we came to Kadesh-barnea.

units.leftText: I said: “You have reached the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.
units.rightText: And I said unto you, Ye are come unto the hill-country of the Amorites, which Jehovah our God giveth unto us.

units.leftText: See, the LORD your God has placed the land before you. Go up and take possession of it as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has told you. Do not be afraid or discouraged.”
units.rightText: Behold, Jehovah thy God hath set the land before thee: go up, take possession, as Jehovah, the God of thy fathers, hath spoken unto thee; fear not, neither be dismayed.

units.leftText: Then all of you approached me and said, “Let us send men ahead of us to search out the land and bring us word of what route to follow and which cities to enter.”
units.rightText: And ye came near unto me every one of you, and said, Let us send men before us, that they may search the land for us, and bring us word again of the way by which we must go up, and the cities unto which we shall come.

units.leftText: The plan seemed good to me, so I selected twelve men from among you, one from each tribe.
units.rightText: And the thing pleased me well; and I took twelve men of you, one man for every tribe:

units.leftText: They left and went up into the hill country, and came to the Valley of Eshcol and spied out the land.
units.rightText: and they turned and went up into the hill-country, and came unto the valley of Eshcol, and spied it out.

units.leftText: They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands, carried it down to us, and brought us word: “It is a good land that the LORD our God is giving us.” Israel’s Rebellion (Numbers 14:1–12|NUM 14:1-12*)
units.rightText: And they took of the fruit of the land in their hands, and brought it down unto us, and brought us word again, and said, It is a good land which Jehovah our God giveth unto us.

units.leftText: But you were unwilling to go up; you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.
units.rightText: Yet ye would not go up, but rebelled against the commandment of Jehovah your God:

units.leftText: You grumbled in your tents and said, “Because the LORD hates us, He has brought us out of the land of Egypt to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites to be annihilated.
units.rightText: and ye murmured in your tents, and said, Because Jehovah hated us, he hath brought us forth out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us.

units.leftText: Where can we go? Our brothers have made our hearts melt, saying: ‘The people are larger and taller than we are; the cities are large, with walls up to the heavens. We even saw the descendants of the Anakim there.’”
units.rightText: Whither are we going up? our brethren have made our heart to melt, saying, The people are greater and taller than we; the cities are great and fortified up to heaven; and moreover we have seen the sons of the Anakim there.

units.leftText: So I said to you: “Do not be terrified or afraid of them!
units.rightText: Then I said unto you, Dread not, neither be afraid of them.

units.leftText: The LORD your God, who goes before you, will fight for you, just as you saw Him do for you in Egypt
units.rightText: Jehovah your God who goeth before you, he will fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Egypt before your eyes,

units.leftText: and in the wilderness, where the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way by which you traveled until you reached this place.”
units.rightText: and in the wilderness, where thou hast seen how that Jehovah thy God bare thee, as a man doth bear his son, in all the way that ye went, until ye came unto this place.

units.leftText: But in spite of all this, you did not trust the LORD your God,
units.rightText: Yet in this thing ye did not believe Jehovah your God,

units.leftText: who went before you on the journey, in the fire by night and in the cloud by day, to seek out a place for you to camp and to show you the road to travel. Israel’s Penalty (Numbers 14:20–35|NUM 14:20-35*)
units.rightText: who went before you in the way, to seek you out a place to pitch your tents in, in fire by night, to show you by what way ye should go, and in the cloud by day.

units.leftText: When the LORD heard your words, He grew angry and swore an oath, saying,
units.rightText: And Jehovah heard the voice of your words, and was wroth, and sware, saying,

units.leftText: “Not one of the men of this evil generation shall see the good land I swore to give your fathers,
units.rightText: Surely there shall not one of these men of this evil generation see the good land, which I sware to give unto your fathers,

units.leftText: except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see it, and I will give him and his descendants the land on which he has set foot, because he followed the LORD wholeheartedly.”
units.rightText: save Caleb the son of Jephunneh; he shall see it; and to him will I give the land that he hath trodden upon, and to his children, because he hath wholly followed Jehovah.

units.leftText: The LORD was also angry with me on your account, and He said, “Not even you shall enter the land.
units.rightText: Also Jehovah was angry with me for your sakes, saying, Thou also shalt not go in thither:

units.leftText: Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, will enter it. Encourage him, for he will enable Israel to inherit the land.
units.rightText: Joshua the son of Nun, who standeth before thee, he shall go in thither: encourage thou him; for he shall cause Israel to inherit it.

units.leftText: And the little ones you said would become captives — your children who on that day did not know good from evil — will enter the land that I will give them, and they will possess it.
units.rightText: Moreover your little ones, that ye said should be a prey, and your children, that this day have no knowledge of good or evil, they shall go in thither, and unto them will I give it, and they shall possess it.

units.leftText: But you are to turn back and head for the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea. ” The Defeat at Hormah (Numbers 14:40–45|NUM 14:40-45*)
units.rightText: But as for you, turn you, and take your journey into the wilderness by the way to the Red Sea.
leftNotes: 1:40 Or the Sea of Reeds

units.leftText: “We have sinned against the LORD,” you replied. “We will go up and fight, as the LORD our God has commanded us.” Then each of you put on his weapons of war, thinking it easy to go up into the hill country.
units.rightText: Then ye answered and said unto me, We have sinned against Jehovah, we will go up and fight, according to all that Jehovah our God commanded us. And ye girded on every man his weapons of war, and were forward to go up into the hill-country.

units.leftText: But the LORD said to me, “Tell them not to go up and fight, for I am not with you to keep you from defeat by your enemies.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto me, Say unto them, Go not up, neither fight; for I am not among you; lest ye be smitten before your enemies.

units.leftText: So I spoke to you, but you would not listen. You rebelled against the command of the LORD and presumptuously went up into the hill country.
units.rightText: So I spake unto you, and ye hearkened not; but ye rebelled against the commandment of Jehovah, and were presumptuous, and went up into the hill-country.

units.leftText: Then the Amorites who lived in the hills came out against you and chased you like a swarm of bees. They routed you from Seir all the way to Hormah.
units.rightText: And the Amorites, that dwelt in that hill-country, came out against you, and chased you, as bees do, and beat you down in Seir, even unto Hormah.

units.leftText: And you returned and wept before the LORD, but He would not listen to your voice or give ear to you.
units.rightText: And ye returned and wept before Jehovah; but Jehovah hearkened not to your voice, nor gave ear unto you.

units.leftText: For this reason you stayed in Kadesh for a long time — a very long time.
units.rightText: So ye abode in Kadesh many days, according unto the days that ye abode there.

units.leftText: Then we turned back and headed for the wilderness by way of the Red Sea, as the LORD had instructed me, and for many days we wandered around Mount Seir.
units.rightText: Then we turned, and took our journey into the wilderness by the way to the Red Sea, as Jehovah spake unto me; and we compassed mount Seir many days.
leftNotes: 2:1 Or the Sea of Reeds

units.leftText: At this time the LORD said to me,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto me, saying,

units.leftText: “You have been wandering around this hill country long enough; turn to the north
units.rightText: Ye have compassed this mountain long enough: turn you northward.

units.leftText: and command the people: ‘You will pass through the territory of your brothers, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, so you must be very careful.
units.rightText: And command thou the people, saying, Ye are to pass through the border of your brethren the children of Esau, that dwell in Seir; and they will be afraid of you. Take ye good heed unto yourselves therefore;

units.leftText: Do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of their land, not even a footprint, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as his possession.
units.rightText: contend not with them; for I will not give you of their land, no, not so much as for the sole of the foot to tread on; because I have given mount Seir unto Esau for a possession.

units.leftText: You are to pay them in silver for the food you eat and the water you drink.’”
units.rightText: Ye shall purchase food of them for money, that ye may eat; and ye shall also buy water of them for money, that ye may drink.

units.leftText: Indeed, the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has watched over your journey through this vast wilderness. The LORD your God has been with you these forty years, and you have lacked nothing.
units.rightText: For Jehovah thy God hath blessed thee in all the work of thy hand; he hath known thy walking through this great wilderness: these forty years Jehovah thy God hath been with thee; thou hast lacked nothing.

units.leftText: So we passed by our brothers, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. We turned away from the Arabah road, which comes up from Elath and Ezion-geber, and traveled along the road of the Wilderness of Moab.
units.rightText: So we passed by from our brethren the children of Esau, that dwell in Seir, from the way of the Arabah from Elath and from Ezion-geber. And we turned and passed by the way of the wilderness of Moab.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to me, “Do not harass the Moabites or provoke them to war, for I will not give you any of their land, because I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as their possession.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto me, Vex not Moab, neither contend with them in battle; for I will not give thee of his land for a possession; because I have given Ar unto the children of Lot for a possession.

units.leftText: (The Emites used to live there, a people great and many, as tall as the Anakites.
units.rightText: (The Emim dwelt therein aforetime, a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakim:

units.leftText: Like the Anakites, they were also regarded as Rephaim, though the Moabites called them Emites.
units.rightText: these also are accounted Rephaim, as the Anakim; but the Moabites call them Emim.

units.leftText: The Horites used to live in Seir, but the descendants of Esau drove them out. They destroyed the Horites from before them and settled in their place, just as Israel did in the land that the LORD gave them as their possession.)
units.rightText: The Horites also dwelt in Seir aforetime, but the children of Esau succeeded them; and they destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their stead; as Israel did unto the land of his possession, which Jehovah gave unto them).

units.leftText: “Now arise and cross over the Brook of Zered.” So we crossed over the Brook of Zered.
units.rightText: Now rise up, and get you over the brook Zered. And we went over the brook Zered.

units.leftText: The time we spent traveling from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed over the Brook of Zered was thirty-eight years, until that entire generation of fighting men had perished from the camp, as the LORD had sworn to them.
units.rightText: And the days in which we came from Kadesh-barnea, until we were come over the brook Zered, were thirty and eight years; until all the generation of the men of war were consumed from the midst of the camp, as Jehovah sware unto them.

units.leftText: Indeed, the LORD’s hand was against them, to eliminate them from the camp, until they had all perished.
units.rightText: Moreover the hand of Jehovah was against them, to destroy them from the midst of the camp, until they were consumed.

units.leftText: Now when all the fighting men among the people had died,
units.rightText: So it came to pass, when all the men of war were consumed and dead from among the people,

units.leftText: the LORD said to me,
units.rightText: that Jehovah spake unto me, saying,

units.leftText: “Today you are going to cross the border of Moab at Ar.
units.rightText: Thou art this day to pass over Ar, the border of Moab:

units.leftText: But when you get close to the Ammonites, do not harass them or provoke them, for I will not give you any of the land of the Ammonites. I have given it to the descendants of Lot as their possession.”
units.rightText: and when thou comest nigh over against the children of Ammon, vex them not, nor contend with them; for I will not give thee of the land of the children of Ammon for a possession; because I have given it unto the children of Lot for a possession.

units.leftText: (That too was regarded as the land of the Rephaim, who used to live there, though the Ammonites called them Zamzummites.
units.rightText: (That also is accounted a land of Rephaim: Rephaim dwelt therein aforetime; but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,

units.leftText: They were a people great and many, as tall as the Anakites. But the LORD destroyed them from before the Ammonites, who drove them out and settled in their place,
units.rightText: a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakim; but Jehovah destroyed them before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead;

units.leftText: just as He had done for the descendants of Esau who lived in Seir, when He destroyed the Horites from before them. They drove them out and have lived in their place to this day.
units.rightText: as he did for the children of Esau, that dwell in Seir, when he destroyed the Horites from before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead even unto this day.

units.leftText: And the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, were destroyed by the Caphtorites, who came out of Caphtor and settled in their place.) The Defeat of Sihon (Numbers 21:21–30|NUM 21:21-30*)
units.rightText: And the Avvim, that dwelt in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorim, that came forth out of Caphtor, destroyed them, and dwelt in their stead.)
leftNotes: 2:23 That is, Crete

units.leftText: “Arise, set out, and cross the Arnon Valley. See, I have delivered into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to take possession of it and engage him in battle.
units.rightText: Rise ye up, take your journey, and pass over the valley of the Arnon: behold, I have given into thy hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land; begin to possess it, and contend with him in battle.

units.leftText: This very day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you upon all the nations under heaven. They will hear the reports of you and tremble in anguish because of you.”
units.rightText: This day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the peoples that are under the whole heaven, who shall hear the report of thee, and shall tremble, and be in anguish because of thee.

units.leftText: So from the Wilderness of Kedemoth I sent messengers with an offer of peace to Sihon king of Heshbon, saying,
units.rightText: And I sent messengers out of the wilderness of Kedemoth unto Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying,

units.leftText: “Let us pass through your land; we will stay on the main road. We will not turn to the right or to the left.
units.rightText: Let me pass through thy land: I will go along by the highway, I will turn neither unto the right hand nor to the left.

units.leftText: You can sell us food to eat and water to drink in exchange for silver. Only let us pass through on foot,
units.rightText: Thou shalt sell me food for money, that I may eat; and give me water for money, that I may drink: only let me pass through on my feet;

units.leftText: just as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for us, until we cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD our God is giving us.”
units.rightText: as the children of Esau that dwell in Seir, and the Moabites that dwell in Ar, did unto me; until I shall pass over the Jordan into the land which Jehovah our God giveth us.

units.leftText: But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass through, for the LORD your God had made his spirit stubborn and his heart obstinate, that He might deliver him into your hand, as is the case this day.
units.rightText: But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass by him; for Jehovah thy God hardened his spirit, and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand, as at this day.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to me, “See, I have begun to deliver Sihon and his land over to you. Now begin to conquer and possess his land.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto me, Behold, I have begun to deliver up Sihon and his land before thee: begin to possess, that thou mayest inherit his land.

units.leftText: So Sihon and his whole army came out for battle against us at Jahaz.
units.rightText: Then Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, unto battle at Jahaz.

units.leftText: And the LORD our God delivered him over to us, and we defeated him and his sons and his whole army.
units.rightText: And Jehovah our God delivered him up before us; and we smote him, and his sons, and all his people.

units.leftText: At that time we captured all his cities and devoted to destruction the people of every city, including women and children. We left no survivors.
units.rightText: And we took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed every inhabited city, with the women and the little ones; we left none remaining:
leftNotes: 2:34 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering.

units.leftText: We carried off for ourselves only the livestock and the plunder from the cities we captured.
units.rightText: only the cattle we took for a prey unto ourselves, with the spoil of the cities which we had taken.

units.leftText: From Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, along with the city in the valley, even as far as Gilead, not one city had walls too high for us. The LORD our God gave us all of them.
units.rightText: From Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and from the city that is in the valley, even unto Gilead, there was not a city too high for us; Jehovah our God delivered up all before us:

units.leftText: But you did not go near the land of the Ammonites, or the land along the banks of the Jabbok River, or the cities of the hill country, or any place that the LORD our God had forbidden.
units.rightText: only to the land of the children of Ammon thou camest not near; all the side of the river Jabbok, and the cities of the hill-country, and wheresoever Jehovah our God forbade us.

units.leftText: Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan and his whole army came out to meet us in battle at Edrei.
units.rightText: Then we turned, and went up the way to Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, unto battle at Edrei.

units.leftText: But the LORD said to me, “Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand, along with all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto me, Fear him not; for I have delivered him, and all his people, and his land, into thy hand; and thou shalt do unto him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt at Heshbon.

units.leftText: So the LORD our God also delivered Og king of Bashan and his whole army into our hands. We struck them down until no survivor was left.
units.rightText: So Jehovah our God delivered into our hand Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we smote him until none was left to him remaining.

units.leftText: At that time we captured all sixty of his cities. There was not a single city we failed to take — the entire region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
units.rightText: And we took all his cities at that time; there was not a city which we took not from them; threescore cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

units.leftText: All these cities were fortified with high walls and gates and bars, and there were many more unwalled villages.
units.rightText: All these were cities fortified with high walls, gates, and bars; besides the unwalled towns a great many.

units.leftText: We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children of every city.
units.rightText: And we utterly destroyed them, as we did unto Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying every inhabited city, with the women and the little ones.

units.leftText: But all the livestock and plunder of the cities we carried off for ourselves.
units.rightText: But all the cattle, and the spoil of the cities, we took for a prey unto ourselves.

units.leftText: At that time we took from the two kings of the Amorites the land across the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley as far as Mount Hermon —
units.rightText: And we took the land at that time out of the hand of the two kings of the Amorites that were beyond the Jordan, from the valley of the Arnon unto mount Hermon

units.leftText: which the Sidonians call Sirion but the Amorites call Senir —

units.leftText: all the cities of the plateau, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as the cities of Salecah and Edrei in the kingdom of Og.
units.rightText: all the cities of the plain, and all Gilead, and all Bashan, unto Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

units.leftText: (For only Og king of Bashan had remained of the remnant of the Rephaim. His bed of iron, nine cubits long and four cubits wide, is still in Rabbah of the Ammonites.) Land Division East of the Jordan (Numbers 32:1–42|NUM 32:1-42*; Joshua 13:8–14|JOS 13:8-14*)
units.rightText: (For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of the Rephaim; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbah of the children of Ammon? nine cubits was the length thereof, and four cubits the breadth of it, after the cubit of a man.)
leftNotes: 3:11 Og’s bed was approximately 14 feet long and 6 feet wide (4.3 meters long and 1.8 meters wide).

units.leftText: So at that time we took possession of this land. To the Reubenites and Gadites I gave the land beyond Aroer along the Arnon Valley, and half the hill country of Gilead, along with its cities.
units.rightText: And this land we took in possession at that time: from Aroer, which is by the valley of the Arnon, and half the hill-country of Gilead, and the cities thereof, gave I unto the Reubenites and to the Gadites:

units.leftText: To the half-tribe of Manasseh I gave the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, the kingdom of Og. (The entire region of Argob, the whole territory of Bashan, used to be called the land of the Rephaim.)
units.rightText: and the rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, gave I unto the half-tribe of Manasseh; all the region of Argob, even all Bashan. (The same is called the land of Rephaim.

units.leftText: Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites. He renamed Bashan after himself, Havvoth-jair, by which it is called to this day.
units.rightText: Jair the son of Manasseh took all the region of Argob, unto the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and called them, even Bashan, after his own name, Havvoth-jair, unto this day.)
leftNotes: 3:14 Or the villages of Jair

units.leftText: To Machir I gave Gilead,
units.rightText: And I gave Gilead unto Machir.

units.leftText: and to the Reubenites and Gadites I gave the territory from Gilead to the Arnon Valley (the middle of the valley was the border) and up to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.
units.rightText: And unto the Reubenites and unto the Gadites I gave from Gilead even unto the valley of the Arnon, the middle of the valley, and the border thereof, even unto the river Jabbok, which is the border of the children of Ammon;

units.leftText: The Jordan River in the Arabah bordered it from Chinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah (the Salt Sea ) with the slopes of Pisgah to the east.
units.rightText: the Arabah also, and the Jordan and the border thereof, from Chinnereth even unto the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah eastward.
leftNotes: 3:17 That is, the Dead Sea

units.leftText: At that time I commanded you: “The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All your men of valor are to cross over, armed for battle, ahead of your brothers, the Israelites.
units.rightText: And I commanded you at that time, saying, Jehovah your God hath given you this land to possess it: ye shall pass over armed before your brethren the children of Israel, all the men of valor.

units.leftText: But your wives, your children, and your livestock— I know that you have much livestock— may remain in the cities I have given you,
units.rightText: But your wives, and your little ones, and your cattle (I know that ye have much cattle), shall abide in your cities which I have given you,

units.leftText: until the LORD gives rest to your brothers as He has to you, and they too have taken possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving them across the Jordan. Then each of you may return to the possession I have given you.”
units.rightText: until Jehovah give rest unto your brethren, as unto you, and they also possess the land which Jehovah your God giveth them beyond the Jordan: then shall ye return every man unto his possession, which I have given you.

units.leftText: And at that time I commanded Joshua: “Your own eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings. The LORD will do the same to all the kingdoms you are about to enter.
units.rightText: And I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, Thine eyes have seen all that Jehovah your God hath done unto these two kings: so shall Jehovah do unto all the kingdoms whither thou goest over.

units.leftText: Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God Himself will fight for you.” Moses Forbidden to Cross the Jordan (Numbers 27:12–17|NUM 27:12-17*)
units.rightText: Ye shall not fear them; for Jehovah your God, he it is that fighteth for you.

units.leftText: At that time I also pleaded with the LORD:
units.rightText: And I besought Jehovah at that time, saying,

units.leftText: “O Lord GOD, You have begun to show Your greatness and power to Your servant. For what god in heaven or on earth can perform such works and mighty acts as Yours?
units.rightText: O Lord Jehovah, thou hast begun to show thy servant thy greatness, and thy strong hand: for what god is there in heaven or in earth, that can do according to thy works, and according to thy mighty acts?

units.leftText: Please let me cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan — that pleasant hill country as well as Lebanon!”
units.rightText: Let me go over, I pray thee, and see the good land that is beyond the Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon.

units.leftText: But the LORD was angry with me on account of you, and He would not listen to me. “That is enough,” the LORD said to me. “Do not speak to Me again about this matter.
units.rightText: But Jehovah was wroth with me for your sakes, and hearkened not unto me; and Jehovah said unto me, Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter.

units.leftText: Go to the top of Pisgah and look to the west and north and south and east. See the land with your own eyes, for you will not cross this Jordan.
units.rightText: Get thee up unto the top of Pisgah, and lift up thine eyes westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and behold with thine eyes: for thou shalt not go over this Jordan.

units.leftText: But commission Joshua, encourage him, and strengthen him, for he will cross over ahead of the people and enable them to inherit the land that you will see.”
units.rightText: But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him; for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which thou shalt see.

units.leftText: So we stayed in the valley opposite Beth-peor.
units.rightText: So we abode in the valley over against Beth-peor.

units.leftText: Hear now, O Israel, the statutes and ordinances I am teaching you to follow, so that you may live and may enter and take possession of the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, is giving you.
units.rightText: And now, O Israel, hearken unto the statutes and unto the ordinances, which I teach you, to do them; that ye may live, and go in and possess the land which Jehovah, the God of your fathers, giveth you.

units.leftText: You must not add to or subtract from what I command you, so that you may keep the commandments of the LORD your God that I am giving you.
units.rightText: Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish from it, that ye may keep the commandments of Jehovah your God which I command you.

units.leftText: Your eyes have seen what the LORD did at Baal-peor, for the LORD your God destroyed from among you all who followed Baal of Peor.
units.rightText: Your eyes have seen what Jehovah did because of Baal-peor; for all the men that followed Baal-peor, Jehovah thy God hath destroyed them from the midst of thee.

units.leftText: But you who held fast to the LORD your God are alive to this day, every one of you.
units.rightText: But ye that did cleave unto Jehovah your God are alive every one of you this day.

units.leftText: See, I have taught you statutes and ordinances just as the LORD my God has commanded me, so that you may follow them in the land that you are about to enter and possess.
units.rightText: Behold, I have taught you statutes and ordinances, even as Jehovah my God commanded me, that ye should do so in the midst of the land whither ye go in to possess it.

units.leftText: Observe them carefully, for this will show your wisdom and understanding in the sight of the peoples, who will hear of all these statutes and say, “Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.”
units.rightText: Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the peoples, that shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.

units.leftText: For what nation is great enough to have a god as near to them as the LORD our God is to us whenever we call on Him?
units.rightText: For what great nation is there, that hath a god so nigh unto them, as Jehovah our God is whensoever we call upon him?

units.leftText: And what nation is great enough to have righteous statutes and ordinances like this entire law I set before you today?
units.rightText: And what great nation is there, that hath statutes and ordinances so righteous as all this law, which I set before you this day?

units.leftText: Only be on your guard and diligently watch yourselves, so that you do not forget the things your eyes have seen, and so that they do not slip from your heart as long as you live. Teach them to your children and grandchildren.
units.rightText: Only take heed to thyself, and keep thy soul diligently, lest thou forget the things which thine eyes saw, and lest they depart from thy heart all the days of thy life; but make them known unto thy children and thy children’s children;

units.leftText: The day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, the LORD said to me, “Gather the people before Me to hear My words, so that they may learn to fear Me all the days they live on the earth, and that they may teach them to their children.”
units.rightText: the day that thou stoodest before Jehovah thy God in Horeb, when Jehovah said unto me, Assemble me the people, and I will make them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children.
leftNotes: 4:10 That is, Mount Sinai, or possibly a mountain in the range containing Mount Sinai; also in verse 15

units.leftText: You came near and stood at the base of the mountain, a mountain blazing with fire to the heavens, with black clouds and deep darkness.
units.rightText: And ye came near and stood under the mountain; and the mountain burned with fire unto the heart of heaven, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

units.leftText: And the LORD spoke to you out of the fire. You heard the sound of the words but saw no form; there was only a voice.
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto you out of the midst of the fire: ye heard the voice of words, but ye saw no form; only ye heard a voice.

units.leftText: He declared to you His covenant, which He commanded you to follow — the Ten Commandments that He wrote on two tablets of stone.
units.rightText: And he declared unto you his covenant, which he commanded you to perform, even the ten commandments; and he wrote them upon two tables of stone.
leftNotes: 4:13 Hebrew the Ten Words

units.leftText: At that time the LORD commanded me to teach you the statutes and ordinances you are to follow in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess. A Warning against Idolatry (Deuteronomy 12:29–32|DEU 12:29-32*; Ezekiel 6:1–7|EZK 6:1-7*)
units.rightText: And Jehovah commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and ordinances, that ye might do them in the land whither ye go over to possess it.

units.leftText: So since you saw no form of any kind on the day the LORD spoke to you out of the fire at Horeb, be careful
units.rightText: Take ye therefore good heed unto yourselves; for ye saw no manner of form on the day that Jehovah spake unto you in Horeb out of the midst of the fire;

units.leftText: that you do not act corruptly and make an idol for yourselves of any form or shape, whether in the likeness of a male or female,
units.rightText: lest ye corrupt yourselves, and make you a graven image in the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female,

units.leftText: of any beast that is on the earth or bird that flies in the air,
units.rightText: the likeness of any beast that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flieth in the heavens,

units.leftText: or of any creature that crawls on the ground or fish that is in the waters below.
units.rightText: the likeness of anything that creepeth on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the water under the earth;

units.leftText: When you look to the heavens and see the sun and moon and stars— all the host of heaven— do not be enticed to bow down and worship what the LORD your God has apportioned to all the nations under heaven.
units.rightText: and lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun and the moon and the stars, even all the host of heaven, thou be drawn away and worship them, and serve them, which Jehovah thy God hath allotted unto all the peoples under the whole heaven.

units.leftText: Yet the LORD has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be the people of His inheritance, as you are today.
units.rightText: But Jehovah hath taken you, and brought you forth out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be unto him a people of inheritance, as at this day.

units.leftText: The LORD, however, was angry with me on account of you, and He swore that I would not cross the Jordan to enter the good land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
units.rightText: Furthermore Jehovah was angry with me for your sakes, and sware that I should not go over the Jordan, and that I should not go in unto that good land, which Jehovah thy God giveth thee for an inheritance:

units.leftText: For I will not be crossing the Jordan, because I must die in this land. But you shall cross over and take possession of that good land.
units.rightText: but I must die in this land, I must not go over the Jordan; but ye shall go over, and possess that good land.

units.leftText: Be careful that you do not forget the covenant of the LORD your God that He made with you; do not make an idol for yourselves in the form of anything He has forbidden you.
units.rightText: Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant of Jehovah your God, which he made with you, and make you a graven image in the form of anything which Jehovah thy God hath forbidden thee.

units.leftText: For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.
units.rightText: For Jehovah thy God is a devouring fire, a jealous God.
leftNotes: 4:24 Cited in Hebrews 12:29|HEB 12:29*

units.leftText: After you have children and grandchildren and you have been in the land a long time, if you then act corruptly and make an idol of any form— doing evil in the sight of the LORD your God and provoking Him to anger—
units.rightText: When thou shalt beget children, and children’s children, and ye shall have been long in the land, and shall corrupt yourselves, and make a graven image in the form of anything, and shall do that which is evil in the sight of Jehovah thy God, to provoke him to anger;

units.leftText: I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you this day that you will quickly perish from the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not live long upon it, but will be utterly destroyed.
units.rightText: I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land whereunto ye go over the Jordan to possess it; ye shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed.

units.leftText: Then the LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and only a few of you will survive among the nations to which the LORD will drive you.
units.rightText: And Jehovah will scatter you among the peoples, and ye shall be left few in number among the nations, whither Jehovah shall lead you away.

units.leftText: And there you will serve man-made gods of wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or eat or smell.
units.rightText: And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.

units.leftText: But if from there you will seek the LORD your God, you will find Him if you seek Him with all your heart and with all your soul.
units.rightText: But from thence ye shall seek Jehovah thy God, and thou shalt find him, when thou searchest after him with all thy heart and with all thy soul.

units.leftText: When you are in distress and all these things have happened to you, then in later days you will return to the LORD your God and listen to His voice.
units.rightText: When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, in the latter days thou shalt return to Jehovah thy God, and hearken unto his voice:

units.leftText: For the LORD your God is a merciful God; He will not abandon you or destroy you or forget the covenant with your fathers, which He swore to them by oath. The LORD Alone Is God
units.rightText: for Jehovah thy God is a merciful God; he will not fail thee, neither destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers which he sware unto them.

units.leftText: Indeed, ask now from one end of the heavens to the other about the days that long preceded you, from the day that God created man on earth: Has anything as great as this ever happened or been reported?
units.rightText: For ask now of the days that are past, which were before thee, since the day that God created man upon the earth, and from the one end of heaven unto the other, whether there hath been any such thing as this great thing is, or hath been heard like it?

units.leftText: Has a people ever heard the voice of God speaking out of the fire, as you have, and lived?
units.rightText: Did ever a people hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as thou hast heard, and live?
leftNotes: 4:33 Or of a god

units.leftText: Or has any god tried to take as his own a nation out of another nation — by trials, signs, wonders, and war, by a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and by great terrors — as the LORD your God did for you in Egypt, before your eyes?
units.rightText: Or hath God assayed to go and take him a nation from the midst of another nation, by trials, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand, and by an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, according to all that Jehovah your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?

units.leftText: You were shown these things so that you would know that the LORD is God; there is no other besides Him.
units.rightText: Unto thee it was showed, that thou mightest know that Jehovah he is God; there is none else besides him.

units.leftText: He let you hear His voice from heaven to discipline you, and on earth He showed you His great fire, and you heard His words out of the fire.
units.rightText: Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice, that he might instruct thee: and upon earth he made thee to see his great fire; and thou heardest his words out of the midst of the fire.

units.leftText: Because He loved your fathers, He chose their descendants after them and brought you out of Egypt by His presence and great power,
units.rightText: And because he loved thy fathers, therefore he chose their seed after them, and brought thee out with his presence, with his great power, out of Egypt;

units.leftText: to drive out before you nations greater and mightier than you, and to bring you into their land and give it to you for your inheritance, as it is this day.
units.rightText: to drive out nations from before thee greater and mightier than thou, to bring thee in, to give thee their land for an inheritance, as at this day.

units.leftText: Know therefore this day and take to heart that the LORD is God in heaven above and on the earth below; there is no other.
units.rightText: Know therefore this day, and lay it to thy heart, that Jehovah he is God in heaven above and upon the earth beneath; there is none else.

units.leftText: Keep His statutes and commandments, which I am giving you today, so that you and your children after you may prosper, and that you may live long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you for all time. Cities of Refuge (Numbers 35:9–34|NUM 35:9-34*; Deuteronomy 19:1–14|DEU 19:1-14*; Joshua 20:1–9|JOS 20:1-9*)
units.rightText: And thou shalt keep his statutes, and his commandments, which I command thee this day, that it may go well with thee, and with thy children after thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days in the land, which Jehovah thy God giveth thee, for ever.

units.leftText: Then Moses set aside three cities across the Jordan to the east
units.rightText: Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan toward the sunrising;

units.leftText: to which a manslayer could flee after killing his neighbor unintentionally without prior malice.
units.rightText: that the manslayer might flee thither, that slayeth his neighbor unawares, and hated him not in time past; and that fleeing unto one of these cities he might live:

units.leftText: Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau belonging to the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead belonging to the Gadites, or Golan in Bashan belonging to the Manassites. Introduction to the Law
units.rightText: namely, Bezer in the wilderness, in the plain country, for the Reubenites; and Ramoth in Gilead, for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan, for the Manassites.

units.leftText: This is the law that Moses set before the Israelites.
units.rightText: And this is the law which Moses set before the children of Israel:

units.leftText: These are the testimonies, statutes, and ordinances that Moses proclaimed to them after they had come out of Egypt,
units.rightText: these are the testimonies, and the statutes, and the ordinances, which Moses spake unto the children of Israel, when they came forth out of Egypt,

units.leftText: while they were in the valley across the Jordan facing Beth-peor in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon and was defeated by Moses and the Israelites after they had come out of Egypt.
units.rightText: beyond the Jordan, in the valley over against Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt at Heshbon, whom Moses and the children of Israel smote, when they came forth out of Egypt.

units.leftText: They took possession of the land belonging to Sihon and to Og king of Bashan — the two Amorite kings across the Jordan to the east —
units.rightText: And they took his land in possession, and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites, who were beyond the Jordan toward the sunrising;

units.leftText: extending from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley as far as Mount Siyon (that is, Hermon),
units.rightText: from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, even unto mount Sion (the same is Hermon),
leftNotes: 4:48 Or Sion; Syriac Sirion

units.leftText: including all the Arabah on the east side of the Jordan and as far as the Sea of the Arabah, below the slopes of Pisgah.
units.rightText: and all the Arabah beyond the Jordan eastward, even unto the sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of Pisgah.
leftNotes: 4:49 That is, the Dead Sea

units.leftText: Then Moses summoned all Israel and said to them:
units.rightText: And Moses called unto all Israel, and said unto them, Hear, O Israel, the statutes and the ordinances which I speak in your ears this day, that ye may learn them, and observe to do them.
leftNotes: 5:1 Note that Deuteronomy 5:1|DEU 5:1* through Deuteronomy 26:19 may be presented as a continuous section of unbroken speech by Moses. In place of multiple levels of nested quotes, this section has been set apart with a double space.

units.leftText: The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
units.rightText: Jehovah our God made a covenant with us in Horeb.
leftNotes: 5:2 That is, Mount Sinai, or possibly a mountain in the range containing Mount Sinai

units.leftText: He did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with all of us who are alive here today.
units.rightText: Jehovah made not this covenant with our fathers, but with us, even us, who are all of us here alive this day.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke with you face to face out of the fire on the mountain. The Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:1–17|EXO 20:1-17*)
units.rightText: Jehovah spake with you face to face in the mount out of the midst of the fire

units.leftText: At that time I was standing between the LORD and you to declare to you the word of the LORD, because you were afraid of the fire and would not go up the mountain. And He said:
units.rightText: (I stood between Jehovah and you at that time, to show you the word of Jehovah: for ye were afraid because of the fire, and went not up into the mount), saying,

units.leftText: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
units.rightText: I am Jehovah thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

units.leftText: You shall have no other gods before Me.
units.rightText: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
leftNotes: 5:7 Or besides Me

units.leftText: You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not make unto thee a graven image, nor any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:

units.leftText: You shall not bow down to them or worship them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me,
units.rightText: thou shalt not bow down thyself unto them, nor serve them; for I, Jehovah, thy God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the third and upon the fourth generation of them that hate me;

units.leftText: but showing loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Me and keep My commandments.
units.rightText: and showing lovingkindness unto thousands of them that love me and keep my commandments.
leftNotes: 5:10 Hebrew loving devotion to thousands; forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not take the name of Jehovah thy God in vain: for Jehovah will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

units.leftText: Observe the Sabbath day by keeping it holy, as the LORD your God has commanded you.
units.rightText: Observe the sabbath day, to keep it holy, as Jehovah thy God commanded thee.

units.leftText: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
units.rightText: Six days shalt thou labor, and do all thy work;

units.leftText: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God, on which you must not do any work— neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your manservant or maidservant, nor your ox or donkey or any of your livestock, nor the foreigner within your gates, so that your manservant and maidservant may rest as you do.
units.rightText: but the seventh day is a sabbath unto Jehovah thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, nor thy man-servant, nor thy maid-servant, nor thine ox, nor thine ass, nor any of thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates; that thy man-servant and thy maid-servant may rest as well as thou.

units.leftText: Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and that the LORD your God brought you out of there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. That is why the LORD your God has commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
units.rightText: And thou shalt remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt, and Jehovah thy God brought thee out thence by a mighty hand and by an outstretched arm: therefore Jehovah thy God commanded thee to keep the sabbath day.

units.leftText: Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God has commanded you, so that your days may be long and that it may go well with you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
units.rightText: Honor thy father and thy mother, as Jehovah thy God commanded thee; that thy days may be long, and that it may go well with thee, in the land which Jehovah thy God giveth thee.
leftNotes: 5:16 Cited in Matthew 15:4|MAT 15:4*, Matthew 19:19, Mark 7:10, Luke 18:20, and Ephesians 6:2–3

units.leftText: You shall not murder.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not kill.
leftNotes: 5:17 Cited in Matthew 5:21|MAT 5:21*, Matthew 19:18, Mark 10:19, Luke 18:20, Romans 13:9, and James 2:11

units.leftText: You shall not commit adultery.
units.rightText: Neither shalt thou commit adultery.
leftNotes: 5:18 Cited in Matthew 5:27|MAT 5:27*, Matthew 19:18, Mark 10:19, Luke 18:20, Romans 13:9, and James 2:11

units.leftText: You shall not steal.
units.rightText: Neither shalt thou steal.
leftNotes: 5:19 Cited in Matthew 19:18|MAT 19:18*, Mark 10:19, Luke 18:20, and Romans 13:9

units.leftText: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
units.rightText: Neither shalt thou bear false witness against thy neighbor.
leftNotes: 5:20 Cited in Matthew 19:18|MAT 19:18*, Mark 10:19, and Luke 18:20

units.leftText: You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife. You shall not covet your neighbor’s house or field, or his manservant or maidservant, or his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.” Moses Intercedes for the People (Exodus 20:18–21|EXO 20:18-21*; Hebrews 12:18–29|HEB 12:18-29*)
units.rightText: Neither shalt thou covet thy neighbor’s wife; neither shalt thou desire thy neighbor’s house, his field, or his man-servant, or his maid-servant, his ox, or his ass, or anything that is thy neighbor’s.
leftNotes: 5:21 Cited in Romans 7:7|ROM 7:7* and Romans 13:9

units.leftText: The LORD spoke these commandments in a loud voice to your whole assembly out of the fire, the cloud, and the deep darkness on the mountain; He added nothing more. And He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
units.rightText: These words Jehovah spake unto all your assembly in the mount out of the midst of the fire, of the cloud, and of the thick darkness, with a great voice: and he added no more. And he wrote them upon two tables of stone, and gave them unto me.

units.leftText: And when you heard the voice out of the darkness while the mountain was blazing with fire, all the heads of your tribes and your elders approached me,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when ye heard the voice out of the midst of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, that ye came near unto me, even all the heads of your tribes, and your elders;

units.leftText: and you said, “Behold, the LORD our God has shown us His glory and greatness, and we have heard His voice out of the fire. Today we have seen that a man can live even if God speaks with him.
units.rightText: and ye said, Behold, Jehovah our God hath showed us his glory and his greatness, and we have heard his voice out of the midst of the fire: we have seen this day that God doth speak with man, and he liveth.

units.leftText: But now, why should we die? For this great fire will consume us, and we will die, if we hear the voice of the LORD our God any longer.
units.rightText: Now therefore why should we die? for this great fire will consume us: if we hear the voice of Jehovah our God any more, then we shall die.

units.leftText: For who of all flesh has heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the fire, as we have, and survived?
units.rightText: For who is there of all flesh, that hath heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as we have, and lived?

units.leftText: Go near and listen to all that the LORD our God says. Then you can tell us everything the LORD our God tells you; we will listen and obey.”
units.rightText: Go thou near, and hear all that Jehovah our God shall say: and speak thou unto us all that Jehovah our God shall speak unto thee; and we will hear it, and do it.

units.leftText: And the LORD heard the words you spoke to me, and He said to me, “I have heard the words that these people have spoken to you. They have done well in all that they have spoken.
units.rightText: And Jehovah heard the voice of your words, when ye spake unto me; and Jehovah said unto me, I have heard the voice of the words of this people, which they have spoken unto thee: they have well said all that they have spoken.

units.leftText: If only they had such a heart to fear Me and keep all My commandments always, so that it might be well with them and with their children forever.
units.rightText: Oh that there were such a heart in them, that they would fear me, and keep all my commandments always, that it might be well with them, and with their children for ever!

units.leftText: Go and tell them: ‘Return to your tents.’
units.rightText: Go say to them, Return ye to your tents.

units.leftText: But you stand here with Me, that I may speak to you all the commandments and statutes and ordinances you are to teach them to follow in the land that I am giving them to possess.”
units.rightText: But as for thee, stand thou here by me, and I will speak unto thee all the commandment, and the statutes, and the ordinances, which thou shalt teach them, that they may do them in the land which I give them to possess it.

units.leftText: So be careful to do as the LORD your God has commanded you; you are not to turn aside to the right or to the left.
units.rightText: Ye shall observe to do therefore as Jehovah your God hath commanded you: ye shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.

units.leftText: You must walk in all the ways that the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live and prosper and prolong your days in the land that you will possess.
units.rightText: Ye shall walk in all the way which Jehovah your God hath commanded you, that ye may live, and that it may be well with you, and that ye may prolong your days in the land which ye shall possess.

units.leftText: These are the commandments and statutes and ordinances that the LORD your God has instructed me to teach you to follow in the land that you are about to enter and possess,
units.rightText: Now this is the commandment, the statutes, and the ordinances, which Jehovah your God commanded to teach you, that ye might do them in the land whither ye go over to possess it;

units.leftText: so that you and your children and grandchildren may fear the LORD your God all the days of your lives by keeping all His statutes and commandments that I give you, and so that your days may be prolonged.
units.rightText: that thou mightest fear Jehovah thy God, to keep all his statutes and his commandments, which I command thee, thou, and thy son, and thy son’s son, all the days of thy life; and that thy days may be prolonged.

units.leftText: Hear, O Israel, and be careful to observe them, so that you may prosper and multiply greatly in a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has promised you.
units.rightText: Hear therefore, O Israel, and observe to do it; that it may be well with thee, and that ye may increase mightily, as Jehovah, the God of thy fathers, hath promised unto thee, in a land flowing with milk and honey.

units.leftText: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One.
units.rightText: Hear, O Israel: Jehovah our God is one Jehovah:
leftNotes: 6:4 Or The LORD our God is One LORD or The LORD is our God, the LORD is One or The LORD is our God, the LORD alone; cited in Mark 12:29|MRK 12:29*

units.leftText: And you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.
units.rightText: and thou shalt love Jehovah thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.
leftNotes: 6:5 Cited in Matthew 22:37|MAT 22:37*, Mark 12:30, and Luke 10:27

units.leftText: These words I am commanding you today are to be upon your hearts.
units.rightText: And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be upon thy heart;

units.leftText: And you shall teach them diligently to your children and speak of them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
units.rightText: and thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thy house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.

units.leftText: Tie them as reminders on your hands and bind them on your foreheads.
units.rightText: And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thy hand, and they shall be for frontlets between thine eyes.

units.leftText: Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates.
units.rightText: And thou shalt write them upon the door-posts of thy house, and upon thy gates.

units.leftText: And when the LORD your God brings you into the land He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, that He would give you— a land with great and splendid cities that you did not build,
units.rightText: And it shall be, when Jehovah thy God shall bring thee into the land which he sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give thee, great and goodly cities, which thou buildest not,

units.leftText: with houses full of every good thing with which you did not fill them, with wells that you did not dig, and with vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant— and when you eat and are satisfied,
units.rightText: and houses full of all good things, which thou filledst not, and cisterns hewn out, which thou hewedst not, vineyards and olive-trees, which thou plantedst not, and thou shalt eat and be full;

units.leftText: be careful not to forget the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
units.rightText: then beware lest thou forget Jehovah, who brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

units.leftText: Fear the LORD your God, serve Him only, and take your oaths in His name.
units.rightText: Thou shalt fear Jehovah thy God; and him shalt thou serve, and shalt swear by his name.
leftNotes: 6:13 Or serve Him, and take your oaths only in His name; cited in Matthew 4:10|MAT 4:10* and Luke 4:8

units.leftText: Do not follow other gods, the gods of the peoples around you.
units.rightText: Ye shall not go after other gods, of the gods of the peoples that are round about you;

units.leftText: For the LORD your God, who is among you, is a jealous God. Otherwise the anger of the LORD your God will be kindled against you, and He will wipe you off the face of the earth.
units.rightText: for Jehovah thy God in the midst of thee is a jealous God; lest the anger of Jehovah thy God be kindled against thee, and he destroy thee from off the face of the earth.

units.leftText: Do not test the LORD your God as you tested Him at Massah.
units.rightText: Ye shall not tempt Jehovah your God, as ye tempted him in Massah.
leftNotes: 6:16 Massah means testing; see Exodus 17:7|EXO 17:7*; cited in Matthew 4:7 and Luke 4:12.

units.leftText: You are to diligently keep the commandments of the LORD your God and the testimonies and statutes He has given you.
units.rightText: Ye shall diligently keep the commandments of Jehovah your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes, which he hath commanded thee.

units.leftText: Do what is right and good in the sight of the LORD, so that it may be well with you and that you may enter and possess the good land that the LORD your God swore to give your fathers,
units.rightText: And thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of Jehovah; that it may be well with thee, and that thou mayest go in and possess the good land which Jehovah sware unto thy fathers,

units.leftText: driving out all your enemies before you, as the LORD has said. Teach Your Children
units.rightText: to thrust out all thine enemies from before thee, as Jehovah hath spoken.

units.leftText: In the future, when your son asks, “What is the meaning of the decrees and statutes and ordinances that the LORD our God has commanded you?”
units.rightText: When thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What mean the testimonies, and the statutes, and the ordinances, which Jehovah our God hath commanded you?

units.leftText: then you are to tell him, “We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt, but the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
units.rightText: then thou shalt say unto thy son, We were Pharaoh’s bondmen in Egypt: and Jehovah brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand;

units.leftText: Before our eyes the LORD inflicted great and devastating signs and wonders on Egypt, on Pharaoh, and on all his household.
units.rightText: and Jehovah showed signs and wonders, great and sore, upon Egypt, upon Pharaoh, and upon all his house, before our eyes;

units.leftText: But He brought us out from there to lead us in and give us the land that He had sworn to our fathers.
units.rightText: and he brought us out from thence, that he might bring us in, to give us the land which he sware unto our fathers.

units.leftText: And the LORD commanded us to observe all these statutes and to fear the LORD our God, that we may always be prosperous and preserved, as we are to this day.
units.rightText: And Jehovah commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear Jehovah our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive, as at this day.

units.leftText: And if we are careful to observe every one of these commandments before the LORD our God, as He has commanded us, then that will be our righteousness.”
units.rightText: And it shall be righteousness unto us, if we observe to do all this commandment before Jehovah our God, as he hath commanded us.

units.leftText: When the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are entering to possess, and He drives out before you many nations— the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, seven nations larger and stronger than you—
units.rightText: When Jehovah thy God shall bring thee into the land whither thou goest to possess it, and shall cast out many nations before thee, the Hittite, and the Girgashite, and the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, seven nations greater and mightier than thou;

units.leftText: and when the LORD your God has delivered them over to you to defeat them, then you must devote them to complete destruction. Make no treaty with them and show them no mercy.
units.rightText: and when Jehovah thy God shall deliver them up before thee, and thou shalt smite them; then thou shalt utterly destroy them: thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor show mercy unto them;
leftNotes: 7:2 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering; also twice in verse 26.
7:2 Forms of the Hebrew berit are translated in most passages as covenant.

units.leftText: Do not intermarry with them. Do not give your daughters to their sons or take their daughters for your sons,
units.rightText: neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.

units.leftText: because they will turn your sons away from following Me to serve other gods. Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and He will swiftly destroy you.
units.rightText: For he will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of Jehovah be kindled against you, and he will destroy thee quickly.

units.leftText: Instead, this is what you are to do to them: tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their idols in the fire.
units.rightText: But thus shall ye deal with them: ye shall break down their altars, and dash in pieces their pillars, and hew down their Asherim, and burn their graven images with fire.

units.leftText: For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you to be a people for His prized possession out of all peoples on the face of the earth.
units.rightText: For thou art a holy people unto Jehovah thy God: Jehovah thy God hath chosen thee to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples that are upon the face of the earth.

units.leftText: The LORD did not set His affection on you and choose you because you were more numerous than the other peoples, for you were the fewest of all peoples.
units.rightText: Jehovah did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; for ye were the fewest of all peoples:

units.leftText: But because the LORD loved you and kept the oath He swore to your fathers, He brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
units.rightText: but because Jehovah loveth you, and because he would keep the oath which he sware unto your fathers, hath Jehovah brought you out with a mighty hand, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.

units.leftText: Know therefore that the LORD your God is God, the faithful God who keeps His covenant of loving devotion for a thousand generations of those who love Him and keep His commandments.
units.rightText: Know therefore that Jehovah thy God, he is God, the faithful God, who keepeth covenant and lovingkindness with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations,

units.leftText: But those who hate Him He repays to their faces with destruction; He will not hesitate to repay to his face the one who hates Him.
units.rightText: and repayeth them that hate him to their face, to destroy them: he will not be slack to him that hateth him, he will repay him to his face.

units.leftText: So keep the commandments and statutes and ordinances that I am giving you to follow this day. The Promises of God (Exodus 23:20–33|EXO 23:20-33*)
units.rightText: Thou shalt therefore keep the commandment, and the statutes, and the ordinances, which I command thee this day, to do them.

units.leftText: If you listen to these ordinances and keep them carefully, then the LORD your God will keep His covenant and the loving devotion that He swore to your fathers.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, because ye hearken to these ordinances, and keep and do them, that Jehovah thy God will keep with thee the covenant and the lovingkindness which he sware unto thy fathers:

units.leftText: He will love you and bless you and multiply you. He will bless the fruit of your womb and the produce of your land— your grain, new wine, and oil, the young of your herds and the lambs of your flocks— in the land that He swore to your fathers to give you.
units.rightText: and he will love thee, and bless thee, and multiply thee; he will also bless the fruit of thy body and the fruit of thy ground, thy grain and thy new wine and thine oil, the increase of thy cattle and the young of thy flock, in the land which he sware unto thy fathers to give thee.

units.leftText: You will be blessed above all peoples; among you there will be no barren man or woman or livestock.
units.rightText: Thou shalt be blessed above all peoples: there shall not be male or female barren among you, or among your cattle.

units.leftText: And the LORD will remove from you all sickness. He will not lay upon you any of the terrible diseases you knew in Egypt, but He will inflict them on all who hate you.
units.rightText: And Jehovah will take away from thee all sickness; and none of the evil diseases of Egypt, which thou knowest, will he put upon thee, but will lay them upon all them that hate thee.

units.leftText: You must destroy all the peoples the LORD your God will deliver to you. Do not look on them with pity. Do not worship their gods, for that will be a snare to you.
units.rightText: And thou shalt consume all the peoples that Jehovah thy God shall deliver unto thee; thine eye shall not pity them: neither shalt thou serve their gods; for that will be a snare unto thee.

units.leftText: You may say in your heart, “These nations are greater than we are; how can we drive them out?”
units.rightText: If thou shalt say in thy heart, These nations are more than I; how can I dispossess them?

units.leftText: But do not be afraid of them. Be sure to remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt:
units.rightText: thou shalt not be afraid of them: thou shalt well remember what Jehovah thy God did unto Pharaoh, and unto all Egypt;

units.leftText: the great trials that you saw, the signs and wonders, and the mighty hand and outstretched arm by which the LORD your God brought you out. The LORD your God will do the same to all the peoples you now fear.
units.rightText: the great trials which thine eyes saw, and the signs, and the wonders, and the mighty hand, and the outstretched arm, whereby Jehovah thy God brought thee out: so shall Jehovah thy God do unto all the peoples of whom thou art afraid.

units.leftText: Moreover, the LORD your God will send the hornet against them until even the survivors hiding from you have perished.
units.rightText: Moreover Jehovah thy God will send the hornet among them, until they that are left, and hide themselves, perish from before thee.

units.leftText: Do not be terrified by them, for the LORD your God, who is among you, is a great and awesome God.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not be affrighted at them; for Jehovah thy God is in the midst of thee, a great God and a terrible.
