units.leftText: The LORD your God will drive out these nations before you little by little. You will not be enabled to eliminate them all at once, or the wild animals would multiply around you.
units.rightText: And Jehovah thy God will cast out those nations before thee by little and little: thou mayest not consume them at once, lest the beasts of the field increase upon thee.

units.leftText: But the LORD your God will give them over to you and throw them into great confusion, until they are destroyed.
units.rightText: But Jehovah thy God will deliver them up before thee, and will discomfit them with a great discomfiture, until they be destroyed.

units.leftText: He will hand their kings over to you, and you will wipe out their names from under heaven. No one will be able to stand against you; you will annihilate them.
units.rightText: And he will deliver their kings into thy hand, and thou shalt make their name to perish from under heaven: there shall no man be able to stand before thee, until thou have destroyed them.

units.leftText: You must burn up the images of their gods; do not covet the silver and gold that is on them or take it for yourselves, or you will be ensnared by it; for it is detestable to the LORD your God.
units.rightText: The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not covet the silver or the gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein; for it is an abomination to Jehovah thy God.

units.leftText: And you must not bring any detestable thing into your house, or you, like it, will be set apart for destruction. You are to utterly detest and abhor it, because it is set apart for destruction.
units.rightText: And thou shalt not bring an abomination into thy house, and become a devoted thing like unto it: thou shalt utterly detest it, and thou shalt utterly abhor it; for it is a devoted thing.

units.leftText: You must carefully follow every commandment I am giving you today, so that you may live and multiply, and enter and possess the land that the LORD swore to give your fathers.
units.rightText: All the commandment which I command thee this day shall ye observe to do, that ye may live, and multiply, and go in and possess the land which Jehovah sware unto your fathers.

units.leftText: Remember that these forty years the LORD your God led you all the way in the wilderness, so that He might humble you and test you in order to know what was in your heart, whether or not you would keep His commandments.
units.rightText: And thou shalt remember all the way which Jehovah thy God hath led thee these forty years in the wilderness, that he might humble thee, to prove thee, to know what was in thy heart, whether thou wouldest keep his commandments, or not.

units.leftText: He humbled you, and in your hunger He gave you manna to eat, which neither you nor your fathers had known, so that you might understand that man does not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
units.rightText: And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by everything that proceedeth out of the mouth of Jehovah doth man live.
leftNotes: 8:3 Cited in Matthew 4:4|MAT 4:4* and Luke 4:4

units.leftText: Your clothing did not wear out and your feet did not swell during these forty years.
units.rightText: Thy raiment waxed not old upon thee, neither did thy foot swell, these forty years.

units.leftText: So know in your heart that just as a man disciplines his son, so the LORD your God disciplines you.
units.rightText: And thou shalt consider in thy heart, that, as a man chasteneth his son, so Jehovah thy God chasteneth thee.

units.leftText: Therefore you shall keep the commandments of the LORD your God, walking in His ways and fearing Him.
units.rightText: And thou shalt keep the commandments of Jehovah thy God, to walk in his ways, and to fear him.

units.leftText: For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of brooks and fountains and springs that flow through the valleys and hills;
units.rightText: For Jehovah thy God bringeth thee into a good land, a land of brooks of water, of fountains and springs, flowing forth in valleys and hills;

units.leftText: a land of wheat, barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates; a land of olive oil and honey;
units.rightText: a land of wheat and barley, and vines and fig-trees and pomegranates; a land of olive-trees and honey;

units.leftText: a land where you will eat food without scarcity, where you will lack nothing; a land whose rocks are iron and whose hills are ready to be mined for copper.
units.rightText: a land wherein thou shalt eat bread without scarceness, thou shalt not lack anything in it; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills thou mayest dig copper.

units.leftText: When you eat and are satisfied, you are to bless the LORD your God for the good land that He has given you.
units.rightText: And thou shalt eat and be full, and thou shalt bless Jehovah thy God for the good land which he hath given thee.

units.leftText: Be careful not to forget the LORD your God by failing to keep His commandments and ordinances and statutes, which I am giving you this day.
units.rightText: Beware lest thou forget Jehovah thy God, in not keeping his commandments, and his ordinances, and his statutes, which I command thee this day:

units.leftText: Otherwise, when you eat and are satisfied, when you build fine houses in which to dwell,
units.rightText: lest, when thou hast eaten and art full, and hast built goodly houses, and dwelt therein;

units.leftText: and when your herds and flocks grow large and your silver and gold increase and all that you have is multiplied,
units.rightText: and when thy herds and thy flocks multiply, and thy silver and thy gold is multiplied, and all that thou hast is multiplied;

units.leftText: then your heart will become proud, and you will forget the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
units.rightText: then thy heart be lifted up, and thou forget Jehovah thy God, who brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage;

units.leftText: He led you through the vast and terrifying wilderness with its venomous snakes and scorpions, a thirsty and waterless land. He brought you water from the rock of flint.
units.rightText: who led thee through the great and terrible wilderness, wherein were fiery serpents and scorpions, and thirsty ground where was no water; who brought thee forth water out of the rock of flint;

units.leftText: He fed you in the wilderness with manna that your fathers had not known, in order to humble you and test you, so that in the end He might cause you to prosper.
units.rightText: who fed thee in the wilderness with manna, which thy fathers knew not; that he might humble thee, and that he might prove thee, to do thee good at thy latter end:

units.leftText: You might say in your heart, “The power and strength of my hands have made this wealth for me.”
units.rightText: and lest thou say in thy heart, My power and the might of my hand hath gotten me this wealth.

units.leftText: But remember that it is the LORD your God who gives you the power to gain wealth, in order to confirm His covenant that He swore to your fathers even to this day.
units.rightText: But thou shalt remember Jehovah thy God, for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth; that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as at this day.

units.leftText: If you ever forget the LORD your God and go after other gods to worship and bow down to them, I testify against you today that you will surely perish.
units.rightText: And it shall be, if thou shalt forget Jehovah thy God, and walk after other gods, and serve them, and worship them, I testify against you this day that ye shall surely perish.

units.leftText: Like the nations that the LORD has destroyed before you, so you will perish if you do not obey the LORD your God.
units.rightText: As the nations that Jehovah maketh to perish before you, so shall ye perish; because ye would not hearken unto the voice of Jehovah your God.

units.leftText: Hear, O Israel: Today you are about to cross the Jordan to go in and dispossess nations greater and stronger than you, with large cities fortified to the heavens.
units.rightText: Hear, O Israel: thou art to pass over the Jordan this day, to go in to dispossess nations greater and mightier than thyself, cities great and fortified up to heaven,

units.leftText: The people are strong and tall, the descendants of the Anakim. You know about them, and you have heard it said, “Who can stand up to the sons of Anak?”
units.rightText: a people great and tall, the sons of the Anakim, whom thou knowest, and of whom thou hast heard say, Who can stand before the sons of Anak?

units.leftText: But understand that today the LORD your God goes across ahead of you as a consuming fire; He will destroy them and subdue them before you. And you will drive them out and annihilate them swiftly, as the LORD has promised you.
units.rightText: Know therefore this day, that Jehovah thy God is he who goeth over before thee as a devouring fire; he will destroy them, and he will bring them down before thee: so shalt thou drive them out, and make them to perish quickly, as Jehovah hath spoken unto thee.

units.leftText: When the LORD your God has driven them out before you, do not say in your heart, “Because of my righteousness the LORD has brought me in to possess this land.” Rather, the LORD is driving out these nations before you because of their wickedness.
units.rightText: Speak not thou in thy heart, after that Jehovah thy God hath thrust them out from before thee, saying, For my righteousness Jehovah hath brought me in to possess this land; whereas for the wickedness of these nations Jehovah doth drive them out from before thee.

units.leftText: It is not because of your righteousness or uprightness of heart that you are going in to possess their land, but it is because of their wickedness that the LORD your God is driving out these nations before you, to keep the promise He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
units.rightText: Not for thy righteousness, or for the uprightness of thy heart, dost thou go in to possess their land; but for the wickedness of these nations Jehovah thy God doth drive them out from before thee, and that he may establish the word which Jehovah sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

units.leftText: Understand, then, that it is not because of your righteousness that the LORD your God is giving you this good land to possess, for you are a stiff-necked people. The Golden Calf (Exodus 32:1–35|EXO 32:1-35*; Acts 7:39–43|ACT 7:39-43*)
units.rightText: Know therefore, that Jehovah thy God giveth thee not this good land to possess it for thy righteousness; for thou art a stiffnecked people.

units.leftText: Remember this, and never forget how you provoked the LORD your God in the wilderness. From the day you left the land of Egypt until you reached this place, you have been rebelling against the LORD.
units.rightText: Remember, forget thou not, how thou provokedst Jehovah thy God to wrath in the wilderness: from the day that thou wentest forth out of the land of Egypt, until ye came unto this place, ye have been rebellious against Jehovah.

units.leftText: At Horeb you provoked the LORD, and He was angry enough to destroy you.
units.rightText: Also in Horeb ye provoked Jehovah to wrath, and Jehovah was angry with you to destroy you.
leftNotes: 9:8 That is, Mount Sinai, or possibly a mountain in the range containing Mount Sinai

units.leftText: When I went up on the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant that the LORD made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.
units.rightText: When I was gone up into the mount to receive the tables of stone, even the tables of the covenant which Jehovah made with you, then I abode in the mount forty days and forty nights; I did neither eat bread nor drink water.

units.leftText: Then the LORD gave me the two stone tablets, inscribed by the finger of God with the exact words that the LORD spoke to you out of the fire on the mountain on the day of the assembly.
units.rightText: And Jehovah delivered unto me the two tables of stone written with the finger of God; and on them was written according to all the words, which Jehovah spake with you in the mount out of the midst of the fire in the day of the assembly.

units.leftText: And at the end of forty days and forty nights, the LORD gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the end of forty days and forty nights, that Jehovah gave me the two tables of stone, even the tables of the covenant.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to me, “Get up and go down from here at once, for your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. How quickly they have turned aside from the way that I commanded them! They have made for themselves a molten image.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto me, Arise, get thee down quickly from hence; for thy people that thou hast brought forth out of Egypt have corrupted themselves; they are quickly turned aside out of the way which I commanded them; they have made them a molten image.

units.leftText: The LORD also said to me, “I have seen this people, and they are indeed a stiff-necked people.
units.rightText: Furthermore Jehovah spake unto me, saying, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people:

units.leftText: Leave Me alone, so that I may destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven. Then I will make you into a nation mightier and greater than they are.”
units.rightText: let me alone, that I may destroy them, and blot out their name from under heaven; and I will make of thee a nation mightier and greater than they.

units.leftText: So I went back down the mountain while it was blazing with fire, with the two tablets of the covenant in my hands.
units.rightText: So I turned and came down from the mount, and the mount was burning with fire: and the two tables of the covenant were in my two hands.

units.leftText: And I saw how you had sinned against the LORD your God; you had made for yourselves a molten calf. You had turned aside quickly from the way that the LORD had commanded you.
units.rightText: And I looked, and, behold, ye had sinned against Jehovah your God; ye had made you a molten calf: ye had turned aside quickly out of the way which Jehovah had commanded you.

units.leftText: So I took the two tablets and threw them out of my hands, shattering them before your eyes.
units.rightText: And I took hold of the two tables, and cast them out of my two hands, and brake them before your eyes.

units.leftText: Then I fell down before the LORD for forty days and forty nights, as I had done the first time. I did not eat bread or drink water because of all the sin you had committed in doing what was evil in the sight of the LORD and provoking Him to anger.
units.rightText: And I fell down before Jehovah, as at the first, forty days and forty nights; I did neither eat bread nor drink water; because of all your sin which ye sinned, in doing that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, to provoke him to anger.

units.leftText: For I was afraid of the anger and wrath that the LORD had directed against you, enough to destroy you. But the LORD listened to me this time as well.
units.rightText: For I was afraid of the anger and hot displeasure, wherewith Jehovah was wroth against you to destroy you. But Jehovah hearkened unto me that time also.
leftNotes: 9:19 LXX And I am greatly terrified; cited in Hebrews 12:21|HEB 12:21*

units.leftText: The LORD was angry enough with Aaron to destroy him, but at that time I also prayed for Aaron.
units.rightText: And Jehovah was very angry with Aaron to destroy him: and I prayed for Aaron also at the same time.

units.leftText: And I took that sinful thing, the calf you had made, and burned it in the fire. Then I crushed it and ground it to powder as fine as dust, and I cast it into the stream that came down from the mountain.
units.rightText: And I took your sin, the calf which ye had made, and burnt it with fire, and stamped it, grinding it very small, until it was as fine as dust: and I cast the dust thereof into the brook that descended out of the mount.

units.leftText: You continued to provoke the LORD at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah.
units.rightText: And at Taberah, and at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah, ye provoked Jehovah to wrath.
leftNotes: 9:22 Taberah means burning; see Numbers 11:3|NUM 11:3*.
9:22 Massah means testing; see Exodus 17:7|EXO 17:7*.
9:22 Kibroth-hattaavah means graves of craving; see Numbers 11:34|NUM 11:34*.

units.leftText: And when the LORD sent you out from Kadesh-barnea, He said, “Go up and possess the land that I have given you.”
units.rightText: And when Jehovah sent you from Kadesh-barnea, saying, Go up and possess the land which I have given you; then ye rebelled against the commandment of Jehovah your God, and ye believed him not, nor hearkened to his voice.

units.leftText: You have been rebelling against the LORD since the day I came to know you.
units.rightText: Ye have been rebellious against Jehovah from the day that I knew you.

units.leftText: So I fell down before the LORD for forty days and forty nights, because the LORD had said He would destroy you.
units.rightText: So I fell down before Jehovah the forty days and forty nights that I fell down, because Jehovah had said he would destroy you.

units.leftText: And I prayed to the LORD and said, “O Lord GOD, do not destroy Your people, Your inheritance, whom You redeemed through Your greatness and brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
units.rightText: And I prayed unto Jehovah, and said, O Lord Jehovah, destroy not thy people and thine inheritance, that thou hast redeemed through thy greatness, that thou hast brought forth out of Egypt with a mighty hand.

units.leftText: Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Overlook the stubbornness of this people and the wickedness of their sin.
units.rightText: Remember thy servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; look not unto the stubbornness of this people, nor to their wickedness, nor to their sin,

units.leftText: Otherwise, those in the land from which You brought us out will say, ‘Because the LORD was not able to bring them into the land He had promised them, and because He hated them, He has brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.’
units.rightText: lest the land whence thou broughtest us out say, Because Jehovah was not able to bring them into the land which he promised unto them, and because he hated them, he hath brought them out to slay them in the wilderness.

units.leftText: But they are Your people, Your inheritance, whom You brought out by Your great power and outstretched arm.”
units.rightText: Yet they are thy people and thine inheritance, which thou broughtest out by thy great power and by thine outstretched arm.

units.leftText: At that time the LORD said to me, “Chisel out two stone tablets like the originals, come up to Me on the mountain, and make an ark of wood.
units.rightText: At that time Jehovah said unto me, Hew thee two tables of stone like unto the first, and come up unto me into the mount, and make thee an ark of wood.

units.leftText: And I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke; and you are to place them in the ark.”
units.rightText: And I will write on the tables the words that were on the first tables which thou brakest, and thou shalt put them in the ark.

units.leftText: So I made an ark of acacia wood, chiseled out two stone tablets like the originals, and went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hands.
units.rightText: So I made an ark of acacia wood, and hewed two tables of stone like unto the first, and went up into the mount, having the two tables in my hand.

units.leftText: And the LORD wrote on the tablets what had been written previously, the Ten Commandments that He had spoken to you on the mountain out of the fire on the day of the assembly. The LORD gave them to me,
units.rightText: And he wrote on the tables, according to the first writing, the ten commandments, which Jehovah spake unto you in the mount out of the midst of the fire in the day of the assembly: and Jehovah gave them unto me.
leftNotes: 10:4 Hebrew the Ten Words

units.leftText: and I went back down the mountain and placed the tablets in the ark I had made, as the LORD had commanded me; and there they have remained.
units.rightText: And I turned and came down from the mount, and put the tables in the ark which I had made; and there they are as Jehovah commanded me.

units.leftText: The Israelites traveled from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son succeeded him as priest.
units.rightText: (And the children of Israel journeyed from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died, and there he was buried; and Eleazar his son ministered in the priest’s office in his stead.
leftNotes: 10:6 Or from the wells of the Bene-jaakan

units.leftText: From there they traveled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land with streams of water.
units.rightText: From thence they journeyed unto Gudgodah; and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of brooks of water.

units.leftText: At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to serve Him, and to pronounce blessings in His name, as they do to this day.
units.rightText: At that time Jehovah set apart the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, to stand before Jehovah to minister unto him, and to bless in his name, unto this day.

units.leftText: That is why Levi has no portion or inheritance among his brothers; the LORD is his inheritance, as the LORD your God promised him.
units.rightText: Wherefore Levi hath no portion nor inheritance with his brethren; Jehovah is his inheritance, according as Jehovah thy God spake unto him.)

units.leftText: I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, like the first time, and that time the LORD again listened to me and agreed not to destroy you.
units.rightText: And I stayed in the mount, as at the first time, forty days and forty nights: and Jehovah hearkened unto me that time also; Jehovah would not destroy thee.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to me, “Get up. Continue your journey ahead of the people, that they may enter and possess the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.” A Call to Obedience (Joshua 24:14–28|JOS 24:14-28*)
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto me, Arise, take thy journey before the people; and they shall go in and possess the land, which I sware unto their fathers to give unto them.

units.leftText: And now, O Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you but to fear the LORD your God by walking in all His ways, to love Him, to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
units.rightText: And now, Israel, what doth Jehovah thy God require of thee, but to fear Jehovah thy God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Jehovah thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul,

units.leftText: and to keep the commandments and statutes of the LORD that I am giving you this day for your own good?
units.rightText: to keep the commandments of Jehovah, and his statutes, which I command thee this day for thy good?

units.leftText: Behold, to the LORD your God belong the heavens, even the highest heavens, and the earth and everything in it.
units.rightText: Behold, unto Jehovah thy God belongeth heaven and the heaven of heavens, the earth, with all that is therein.

units.leftText: Yet the LORD has set His affection on your fathers and loved them. And He has chosen you, their descendants after them, above all the peoples, even to this day.
units.rightText: Only Jehovah had a delight in thy fathers to love them, and he chose their seed after them, even you above all peoples, as at this day.

units.leftText: Circumcise your hearts, therefore, and stiffen your necks no more.
units.rightText: Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.

units.leftText: For the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and awesome God, showing no partiality and accepting no bribe.
units.rightText: For Jehovah your God, he is God of gods, and Lord of lords, the great God, the mighty, and the terrible, who regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward.

units.leftText: He executes justice for the fatherless and widow, and He loves the foreigner, giving him food and clothing.
units.rightText: He doth execute justice for the fatherless and widow, and loveth the sojourner, in giving him food and raiment.

units.leftText: So you also must love the foreigner, since you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: Love ye therefore the sojourner; for ye were sojourners in the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: You are to fear the LORD your God and serve Him. Hold fast to Him and take your oaths in His name.
units.rightText: Thou shalt fear Jehovah thy God; him shalt thou serve; and to him shalt thou cleave, and by his name shalt thou swear.

units.leftText: He is your praise and He is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome wonders that your eyes have seen.
units.rightText: He is thy praise, and he is thy God, that hath done for thee these great and terrible things, which thine eyes have seen.

units.leftText: Your fathers went down to Egypt, seventy in all, and now the LORD your God has made you as numerous as the stars in the sky.
units.rightText: Thy fathers went down into Egypt with threescore and ten persons; and now Jehovah thy God hath made thee as the stars of heaven for multitude.

units.leftText: You shall therefore love the LORD your God and always keep His charge, His statutes, His ordinances, and His commandments.
units.rightText: Therefore thou shalt love Jehovah thy God, and keep his charge, and his statutes, and his ordinances, and his commandments, alway.

units.leftText: Know this day that it is not your children who have known and seen the discipline of the LORD your God: His greatness, His mighty hand, and His outstretched arm;
units.rightText: And know ye this day: for I speak not with your children that have not known, and that have not seen the chastisement of Jehovah your God, his greatness, his mighty hand, and his outstretched arm,

units.leftText: the signs and works He did in Egypt to Pharaoh king of Egypt and all his land;
units.rightText: and his signs, and his works, which he did in the midst of Egypt unto Pharaoh the king of Egypt, and unto all his land;

units.leftText: what He did to the Egyptian army and horses and chariots when He made the waters of the Red Sea engulf them as they pursued you, and how He destroyed them completely, even to this day;
units.rightText: and what he did unto the army of Egypt, unto their horses, and to their chariots; how he made the water of the Red Sea to overflow them as they pursued after you, and how Jehovah hath destroyed them unto this day;
leftNotes: 11:4 Or the Sea of Reeds

units.leftText: what He did for you in the wilderness until you reached this place;
units.rightText: and what he did unto you in the wilderness, until ye came unto this place;

units.leftText: and what He did in the midst of all the Israelites to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab the Reubenite, when the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, their tents, and every living thing that belonged to them.
units.rightText: and what he did unto Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, the son of Reuben; how the earth opened its mouth, and swallowed them up, and their households, and their tents, and every living thing that followed them, in the midst of all Israel:

units.leftText: For it is your own eyes that have seen every great work that the LORD has done. God’s Great Blessings (Joshua 1:1–9|JOS 1:1-9*)
units.rightText: but your eyes have seen all the great work of Jehovah which he did.

units.leftText: You shall therefore keep every commandment I am giving you today, so that you may have the strength to go in and possess the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess,
units.rightText: Therefore shall ye keep all the commandment which I command thee this day, that ye may be strong, and go in and possess the land, whither ye go over to possess it;

units.leftText: and so that you may live long in the land that the LORD swore to your fathers to give them and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
units.rightText: and that ye may prolong your days in the land, which Jehovah sware unto your fathers to give unto them and to their seed, a land flowing with milk and honey.

units.leftText: For the land that you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt, from which you have come, where you sowed your seed and irrigated on foot, like a vegetable garden.
units.rightText: For the land, whither thou goest in to possess it, is not as the land of Egypt, from whence ye came out, where thou sowedst thy seed, and wateredst it with thy foot, as a garden of herbs;

units.leftText: But the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess is a land of mountains and valleys that drinks in the rain from heaven.
units.rightText: but the land, whither ye go over to possess it, is a land of hills and valleys, and drinketh water of the rain of heaven,

units.leftText: It is a land for which the LORD your God cares; the eyes of the LORD your God are always on it, from the beginning to the end of the year.
units.rightText: a land which Jehovah thy God careth for: the eyes of Jehovah thy God are always upon it, from the beginning of the year even unto the end of the year.

units.leftText: So if you carefully obey the commandments I am giving you today, to love the LORD your God and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul,
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, if ye shall hearken diligently unto my commandments which I command you this day, to love Jehovah your God, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul,

units.leftText: then I will provide rain for your land in season, the autumn and spring rains, that you may gather your grain, new wine, and oil.
units.rightText: that I will give the rain of your land in its season, the former rain and the latter rain, that thou mayest gather in thy grain, and thy new wine, and thine oil.
leftNotes: 11:14 Hebrew; SP, LXX, and Vulgate He will provide; also in verse 15

units.leftText: And I will provide grass in the fields for your livestock, and you will eat and be satisfied.
units.rightText: And I will give grass in thy fields for thy cattle, and thou shalt eat and be full.

units.leftText: But be careful that you are not enticed to turn aside to worship and bow down to other gods,
units.rightText: Take heed to yourselves, lest your heart be deceived, and ye turn aside, and serve other gods, and worship them;

units.leftText: or the anger of the LORD will be kindled against you. He will shut the heavens so that there will be no rain, nor will the land yield its produce, and you will soon perish from the good land that the LORD is giving you. Remember God’s Words
units.rightText: and the anger of Jehovah be kindled against you, and he shut up the heavens, so that there shall be no rain, and the land shall not yield its fruit; and ye perish quickly from off the good land which Jehovah giveth you.

units.leftText: Fix these words of mine in your hearts and minds; tie them as reminders on your hands and bind them on your foreheads.
units.rightText: Therefore shall ye lay up these my words in your heart and in your soul; and ye shall bind them for a sign upon your hand, and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes.

units.leftText: Teach them to your children, speaking about them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
units.rightText: And ye shall teach them your children, talking of them, when thou sittest in thy house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.

units.leftText: Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates,
units.rightText: And thou shalt write them upon the door-posts of thy house, and upon thy gates;

units.leftText: so that as long as the heavens are above the earth, your days and those of your children may be multiplied in the land that the LORD swore to give your fathers.
units.rightText: that your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, in the land which Jehovah sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of the heavens above the earth.

units.leftText: For if you carefully keep all these commandments I am giving you to follow— to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, and to hold fast to Him—
units.rightText: For if ye shall diligently keep all this commandment which I command you, to do it, to love Jehovah your God, to walk in all his ways, and to cleave unto him;

units.leftText: then the LORD will drive out all these nations before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and stronger than you.
units.rightText: then will Jehovah drive out all these nations from before you, and ye shall dispossess nations greater and mightier than yourselves.

units.leftText: Every place where the sole of your foot treads will be yours. Your territory will extend from the wilderness to Lebanon, and from the Euphrates River to the Western Sea.
units.rightText: Every place whereon the sole of your foot shall tread shall be yours: from the wilderness, and Lebanon, from the river, the river Euphrates, even unto the hinder sea shall be your border.
leftNotes: 11:24 That is, the Mediterranean Sea, also called the Great Sea

units.leftText: No man will be able to stand against you; the LORD your God will put the fear and dread of you upon all the land, wherever you set foot, as He has promised you. A Blessing and a Curse
units.rightText: There shall no man be able to stand before you: Jehovah your God shall lay the fear of you and the dread of you upon all the land that ye shall tread upon, as he hath spoken unto you.

units.leftText: See, today I am setting before you a blessing and a curse —
units.rightText: Behold, I set before you this day a blessing and a curse:

units.leftText: a blessing if you obey the commandments of the LORD your God that I am giving you today,
units.rightText: the blessing, if ye shall hearken unto the commandments of Jehovah your God, which I command you this day;

units.leftText: but a curse if you disobey the commandments of the LORD your God and turn aside from the path I command you today by following other gods, which you have not known.
units.rightText: and the curse, if ye shall not hearken unto the commandments of Jehovah your God, but turn aside out of the way which I command you this day, to go after other gods, which ye have not known.

units.leftText: When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess, you are to proclaim the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, when Jehovah thy God shall bring thee into the land whither thou goest to possess it, that thou shalt set the blessing upon mount Gerizim, and the curse upon mount Ebal.

units.leftText: Are not these mountains across the Jordan, west of the road toward the sunset, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah opposite Gilgal near the Oak of Moreh?
units.rightText: Are they not beyond the Jordan, behind the way of the going down of the sun, in the land of the Canaanites that dwell in the Arabah, over against Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?
leftNotes: 11:30 SP, LXX, and Syriac (see Genesis 12:6|GEN 12:6*); Hebrew Oaks or Terebinths or Great Trees

units.leftText: For you are about to cross the Jordan to enter and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you. When you take possession of it and settle in it,
units.rightText: For ye are to pass over the Jordan to go in to possess the land which Jehovah your God giveth you, and ye shall possess it, and dwell therein.

units.leftText: be careful to follow all the statutes and ordinances that I am setting before you today.
units.rightText: And ye shall observe to do all the statutes and the ordinances which I set before you this day.

units.leftText: These are the statutes and ordinances you must be careful to follow all the days you live in the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you to possess.
units.rightText: These are the statutes and the ordinances which ye shall observe to do in the land which Jehovah, the God of thy fathers, hath given thee to possess it, all the days that ye live upon the earth.

units.leftText: Destroy completely all the places where the nations you are dispossessing have served their gods— atop the high mountains, on the hills, and under every green tree.
units.rightText: Ye shall surely destroy all the places wherein the nations that ye shall dispossess served their gods, upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under every green tree:

units.leftText: Tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, burn up their Asherah poles, cut down the idols of their gods, and wipe out their names from every place.
units.rightText: and ye shall break down their altars, and dash in pieces their pillars, and burn their Asherim with fire; and ye shall hew down the graven images of their gods; and ye shall destroy their name out of that place.

units.leftText: You shall not worship the LORD your God in this way.
units.rightText: Ye shall not do so unto Jehovah your God.

units.leftText: Instead, you must seek the place the LORD your God will choose from among all your tribes to establish as a dwelling for His Name, and there you must go.
units.rightText: But unto the place which Jehovah your God shall choose out of all your tribes, to put his name there, even unto his habitation shall ye seek, and thither thou shalt come;

units.leftText: To that place you are to bring your burnt offerings and sacrifices, your tithes and heave offerings, your vow offerings and freewill offerings, as well as the firstborn of your herds and flocks.
units.rightText: and thither ye shall bring your burnt-offerings, and your sacrifices, and your tithes, and the heave-offering of your hand, and your vows, and your freewill-offerings, and the firstlings of your herd and of your flock:

units.leftText: There, in the presence of the LORD your God, you and your households shall eat and rejoice in all you do, because the LORD your God has blessed you.
units.rightText: and there ye shall eat before Jehovah your God, and ye shall rejoice in all that ye put your hand unto, ye and your households, wherein Jehovah thy God hath blessed thee.

units.leftText: You are not to do as we are doing here today, where everyone does what seems right in his own eyes.
units.rightText: Ye shall not do after all the things that we do here this day, every man whatsoever is right in his own eyes;

units.leftText: For you have not yet come to the resting place and the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.
units.rightText: for ye are not as yet come to the rest and to the inheritance, which Jehovah thy God giveth thee.

units.leftText: When you cross the Jordan and live in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and He gives you rest from all the enemies around you and you dwell securely,
units.rightText: But when ye go over the Jordan, and dwell in the land which Jehovah your God causeth you to inherit, and he giveth you rest from all your enemies round about, so that ye dwell in safety;

units.leftText: then the LORD your God will choose a dwelling for His Name. And there you are to bring everything I command you: your burnt offerings and sacrifices, your tithes and special gifts, and all the choice offerings you vow to the LORD.
units.rightText: then it shall come to pass that to the place which Jehovah your God shall choose, to cause his name to dwell there, thither shall ye bring all that I command you: your burnt-offerings, and your sacrifices, your tithes, and the heave-offering of your hand, and all your choice vows which ye vow unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: And you shall rejoice before the LORD your God— you, your sons and daughters, your menservants and maidservants, and the Levite within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.
units.rightText: And ye shall rejoice before Jehovah your God, ye, and your sons, and your daughters, and your men-servants, and your maid-servants, and the Levite that is within your gates, forasmuch as he hath no portion nor inheritance with you.

units.leftText: Be careful not to offer your burnt offerings in just any place you see;
units.rightText: Take heed to thyself that thou offer not thy burnt-offerings in every place that thou seest;

units.leftText: you must offer them only in the place the LORD will choose in one of your tribal territories, and there you shall do all that I command you.
units.rightText: but in the place which Jehovah shall choose in one of thy tribes, there thou shalt offer thy burnt-offerings, and there thou shalt do all that I command thee.

units.leftText: But whenever you want, you may slaughter and eat meat within any of your gates, according to the blessing the LORD your God has given you. Both the ceremonially clean and unclean may eat it as they would a gazelle or deer,
units.rightText: Notwithstanding, thou mayest kill and eat flesh within all thy gates, after all the desire of thy soul, according to the blessing of Jehovah thy God which he hath given thee: the unclean and the clean may eat thereof, as of the gazelle, and as of the hart.

units.leftText: but you must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.
units.rightText: Only ye shall not eat the blood; thou shalt pour it out upon the earth as water.

units.leftText: Within your gates you must not eat the tithe of your grain or new wine or oil, the firstborn of your herds or flocks, any of the offerings that you have vowed to give, or your freewill offerings or special gifts.
units.rightText: Thou mayest not eat within thy gates the tithe of thy grain, or of thy new wine, or of thine oil, or the firstlings of thy herd or of thy flock, nor any of thy vows which thou vowest, nor thy freewill-offerings, nor the heave-offering of thy hand;

units.leftText: Instead, you must eat them in the presence of the LORD your God at the place the LORD your God will choose— you, your sons and daughters, your menservants and maidservants, and the Levite within your gates. Rejoice before the LORD your God in all you do,
units.rightText: but thou shalt eat them before Jehovah thy God in the place which Jehovah thy God shall choose, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter, and thy man-servant, and thy maid-servant, and the Levite that is within thy gates: and thou shalt rejoice before Jehovah thy God in all that thou puttest thy hand unto.

units.leftText: and be careful not to neglect the Levites as long as you live in your land.
units.rightText: Take heed to thyself that thou forsake not the Levite as long as thou livest in thy land.

units.leftText: When the LORD your God expands your territory as He has promised, and you crave meat and say, “I want to eat meat,” you may eat it whenever you want.
units.rightText: When Jehovah thy God shall enlarge thy border, as he hath promised thee, and thou shalt say, I will eat flesh, because thy soul desireth to eat flesh; thou mayest eat flesh, after all the desire of thy soul.

units.leftText: If the place where the LORD your God chooses to put His Name is too far from you, then you may slaughter any of the herd or flock He has given you, as I have commanded you, and you may eat it within your gates whenever you want.
units.rightText: If the place which Jehovah thy God shall choose, to put his name there, be too far from thee, then thou shalt kill of thy herd and of thy flock, which Jehovah hath given thee, as I have commanded thee; and thou mayest eat within thy gates, after all the desire of thy soul.

units.leftText: Indeed, you may eat it as you would eat a gazelle or deer; both the ceremonially unclean and the clean may eat it.
units.rightText: Even as the gazelle and as the hart is eaten, so thou shalt eat thereof: the unclean and the clean may eat thereof alike.

units.leftText: Only be sure not to eat the blood, because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.
units.rightText: Only be sure that thou eat not the blood: for the blood is the life; and thou shalt not eat the life with the flesh.

units.leftText: You must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not eat it; thou shalt pour it out upon the earth as water.

units.leftText: Do not eat it, so that it may go well with you and your children after you, because you will be doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not eat it; that it may go well with thee, and with thy children after thee, when thou shalt do that which is right in the eyes of Jehovah.

units.leftText: But you are to take your holy things and your vow offerings and go to the place the LORD will choose.
units.rightText: Only thy holy things which thou hast, and thy vows, thou shalt take, and go unto the place which Jehovah shall choose;

units.leftText: Present the meat and blood of your burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD your God. The blood of your other sacrifices must be poured out beside the altar of the LORD your God, but you may eat the meat.
units.rightText: and thou shalt offer thy burnt-offerings, the flesh and the blood, upon the altar of Jehovah thy God; and the blood of thy sacrifices shall be poured out upon the altar of Jehovah thy God; and thou shalt eat the flesh.

units.leftText: Be careful to obey all these things I command you, so that it may always go well with you and your children after you, because you will be doing what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD your God. A Warning against Idolatry (Deuteronomy 4:15–31|DEU 4:15-31*; Ezekiel 6:1–7|EZK 6:1-7*)
units.rightText: Observe and hear all these words which I command thee, that it may go well with thee, and with thy children after thee for ever, when thou doest that which is good and right in the eyes of Jehovah thy God.

units.leftText: When the LORD your God cuts off before you the nations you are entering to dispossess, and you drive them out and live in their land,
units.rightText: When Jehovah thy God shall cut off the nations from before thee, whither thou goest in to dispossess them, and thou dispossessest them, and dwellest in their land;

units.leftText: be careful not to be ensnared by their ways after they have been destroyed before you. Do not inquire about their gods, asking, “How do these nations serve their gods? I will do likewise.”
units.rightText: take heed to thyself that thou be not ensnared to follow them, after that they are destroyed from before thee; and that thou inquire not after their gods, saying, How do these nations serve their gods? even so will I do likewise.

units.leftText: You must not worship the LORD your God in this way, because they practice for their gods every abomination which the LORD hates. They even burn their sons and daughters in the fire as sacrifices to their gods.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not do so unto Jehovah thy God: for every abomination to Jehovah, which he hateth, have they done unto their gods; for even their sons and their daughters do they burn in the fire to their gods.

units.leftText: See that you do everything I command you; do not add to it or subtract from it.
units.rightText: What thing soever I command you, that shall ye observe to do: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it.

units.leftText: If a prophet or dreamer of dreams arises among you and proclaims a sign or wonder to you,
units.rightText: If there arise in the midst of thee a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and he give thee a sign or a wonder,

units.leftText: and if the sign or wonder he has spoken to you comes about, but he says, “Let us follow other gods (which you have not known) and let us worship them,”
units.rightText: and the sign or the wonder come to pass, whereof he spake unto thee, saying, Let us go after other gods, which thou hast not known, and let us serve them;

units.leftText: you must not listen to the words of that prophet or dreamer. For the LORD your God is testing you to find out whether you love Him with all your heart and with all your soul.
units.rightText: thou shalt not hearken unto the words of that prophet, or unto that dreamer of dreams: for Jehovah your God proveth you, to know whether ye love Jehovah your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

units.leftText: You are to follow the LORD your God and fear Him. Keep His commandments and listen to His voice; serve Him and hold fast to Him.
units.rightText: Ye shall walk after Jehovah your God, and fear him, and keep his commandments, and obey his voice, and ye shall serve him, and cleave unto him.

units.leftText: Such a prophet or dreamer must be put to death, because he has advocated rebellion against the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery; he has tried to turn you from the way in which the LORD your God has commanded you to walk. So you must purge the evil from among you.
units.rightText: And that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death, because he hath spoken rebellion against Jehovah your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed thee out of the house of bondage, to draw thee aside out of the way which Jehovah thy God commanded thee to walk in. So shalt thou put away the evil from the midst of thee.
leftNotes: 13:5 Cited in 1 Corinthians 5:13|1CO 5:13*

units.leftText: If your very own brother, or your son or daughter, or the wife you embrace, or your closest friend secretly entices you, saying, “Let us go and worship other gods” (which neither you nor your fathers have known,
units.rightText: If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, that is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers;
leftNotes: 13:6 Hebrew the wife of your bosom

units.leftText: the gods of the peoples around you, whether near or far, whether from one end of the earth or the other),
units.rightText: of the gods of the peoples that are round about you, nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth;

units.leftText: you must not yield to him or listen to him. Show him no pity, and do not spare him or shield him.
units.rightText: thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him:

units.leftText: Instead, you must surely kill him. Your hand must be the first against him to put him to death, and then the hands of all the people.
units.rightText: but thou shalt surely kill him; thy hand shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people.

units.leftText: Stone him to death for trying to turn you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
units.rightText: And thou shalt stone him to death with stones, because he hath sought to draw thee away from Jehovah thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

units.leftText: Then all Israel will hear and be afraid, and will never again do such a wicked thing among you. Idolatrous Cities to Be Destroyed
units.rightText: And all Israel shall hear, and fear, and shall do no more any such wickedness as this is in the midst of thee.

units.leftText: If, regarding one of the cities the LORD your God is giving you to inhabit, you hear it said
units.rightText: If thou shalt hear tell concerning one of thy cities, which Jehovah thy God giveth thee to dwell there, saying,

units.leftText: that wicked men have arisen from among you and have led the people of their city astray, saying, “Let us go and serve other gods” (which you have not known),
units.rightText: Certain base fellows are gone out from the midst of thee, and have drawn away the inhabitants of their city, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which ye have not known;

units.leftText: then you must inquire, investigate, and interrogate thoroughly. And if it is established with certainty that this abomination has been committed among you,
units.rightText: then shalt thou inquire, and make search, and ask diligently; and, behold, if it be truth, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought in the midst of thee,

units.leftText: you must surely put the inhabitants of that city to the sword. Devote to destruction all its people and livestock.
units.rightText: thou shalt surely smite the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, destroying it utterly, and all that is therein and the cattle thereof, with the edge of the sword.
leftNotes: 13:15 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering; similarly in verse 17.

units.leftText: And you are to gather all its plunder in the middle of the public square, and completely burn the city and all its plunder as a whole burnt offering to the LORD your God. The city must remain a mound of ruins forever, never to be rebuilt.
units.rightText: And thou shalt gather all the spoil of it into the midst of the street thereof, and shalt burn with fire the city, and all the spoil thereof every whit, unto Jehovah thy God: and it shall be a heap for ever; it shall not be built again.

units.leftText: Nothing devoted to destruction shall cling to your hands, so that the LORD will turn from His fierce anger, grant you mercy, show you compassion, and multiply you as He swore to your fathers,
units.rightText: And there shall cleave nought of the devoted thing to thy hand; that Jehovah may turn from the fierceness of his anger, and show thee mercy, and have compassion upon thee, and multiply thee, as he hath sworn unto thy fathers;

units.leftText: because you obey the LORD your God, keeping all His commandments I am giving you today and doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
units.rightText: when thou shalt hearken to the voice of Jehovah thy God, to keep all his commandments which I command thee this day, to do that which is right in the eyes of Jehovah thy God.

units.leftText: You are sons of the LORD your God; do not cut yourselves or shave your foreheads on behalf of the dead,
units.rightText: Ye are the children of Jehovah your God: ye shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes for the dead.

units.leftText: for you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD has chosen you to be a people for His prized possession out of all the peoples on the face of the earth.
units.rightText: For thou art a holy people unto Jehovah thy God, and Jehovah hath chosen thee to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples that are upon the face of the earth.

units.leftText: You must not eat any detestable thing.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing.

units.leftText: These are the animals that you may eat: The ox, the sheep, the goat,
units.rightText: These are the beasts which ye may eat: the ox, the sheep, and the goat,
leftNotes: 14:4 The precise identification of some of the birds and animals in this chapter is uncertain.

units.leftText: the deer, the gazelle, the roe deer, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.
units.rightText: the hart, and the gazelle, and the roebuck, and the wild goat, and the pygarg, and the antelope, and the chamois.

units.leftText: You may eat any animal that has a split hoof divided in two and that chews the cud.
units.rightText: And every beast that parteth the hoof, and hath the hoof cloven in two, and cheweth the cud, among the beasts, that may ye eat.

units.leftText: But of those that chew the cud or have a completely divided hoof, you are not to eat the following: the camel, the rabbit, or the rock badger.
units.rightText: Nevertheless these ye shall not eat of them that chew the cud, or of them that have the hoof cloven: the camel, and the hare, and the coney; because they chew the cud but part not the hoof, they are unclean unto you.
leftNotes: 14:7 Or the coney or the hyrax

units.leftText: as well as the pig; though it has a divided hoof, it does not chew the cud. It is unclean for you. You must not eat its meat or touch its carcass.
units.rightText: And the swine, because he parteth the hoof but cheweth not the cud, he is unclean unto you: of their flesh ye shall not eat, and their carcasses ye shall not touch.

units.leftText: Of all the creatures that live in the water, you may eat anything with fins and scales,
units.rightText: These ye may eat of all that are in the waters: whatsoever hath fins and scales may ye eat;

units.leftText: but you may not eat anything that does not have fins and scales; it is unclean for you.
units.rightText: and whatsoever hath not fins and scales ye shall not eat; it is unclean unto you.

units.leftText: You may eat any clean bird,
units.rightText: Of all clean birds ye may eat.

units.leftText: but these you may not eat: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
units.rightText: But these are they of which ye shall not eat: the eagle, and the gier-eagle, and the ospray,

units.leftText: the red kite, the falcon, any kind of kite,
units.rightText: and the glede, and the falcon, and the kite after its kind,

units.leftText: any kind of raven,
units.rightText: and every raven after its kind,

units.leftText: the ostrich, the screech owl, the gull, any kind of hawk,
units.rightText: and the ostrich, and the night-hawk, and the sea-mew, and the hawk after its kind,
leftNotes: 14:15 Literally the daughter of the ostrich or the daughter of the owl

units.leftText: the little owl, the great owl, the white owl,
units.rightText: the little owl, and the great owl, and the horned owl,

units.leftText: the desert owl, the osprey, the cormorant,
units.rightText: and the pelican, and the vulture, and the cormorant,

units.leftText: the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, or the bat.
units.rightText: and the stork, and the heron after its kind, and the hoopoe, and the bat.

units.leftText: All flying insects are unclean for you; they may not be eaten.
units.rightText: And all winged creeping things are unclean unto you: they shall not be eaten.

units.leftText: But you may eat any clean bird.
units.rightText: Of all clean birds ye may eat.

units.leftText: You are not to eat any carcass; you may give it to the foreigner residing within your gates, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner. For you are a holy people belonging to the LORD your God. You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk. Giving Tithes (Leviticus 27:30–34|LEV 27:30-34*; Deuteronomy 26:1–15|DEU 26:1-15*; Nehemiah 13:10–14|NEH 13:10-14*)
units.rightText: Ye shall not eat of anything that dieth of itself: thou mayest give it unto the sojourner that is within thy gates, that he may eat it; or thou mayest sell it unto a foreigner: for thou art a holy people unto Jehovah thy God. Thou shalt not boil a kid in its mother’s milk.

units.leftText: You must be sure to set aside a tenth of all the produce brought forth each year from your fields.
units.rightText: Thou shalt surely tithe all the increase of thy seed, that which cometh forth from the field year by year.

units.leftText: And you are to eat a tenth of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks, in the presence of the LORD your God at the place He will choose as a dwelling for His Name, so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God always.
units.rightText: And thou shalt eat before Jehovah thy God, in the place which he shall choose, to cause his name to dwell there, the tithe of thy grain, of thy new wine, and of thine oil, and the firstlings of thy herd and of thy flock; that thou mayest learn to fear Jehovah thy God always.

units.leftText: But if the distance is too great for you to carry that with which the LORD your God has blessed you, because the place where the LORD your God will choose to put His Name is too far away,
units.rightText: And if the way be too long for thee, so that thou art not able to carry it, because the place is too far from thee, which Jehovah thy God shall choose, to set his name there, when Jehovah thy God shall bless thee;

units.leftText: then exchange it for money, take the money in your hand, and go to the place the LORD your God will choose.
units.rightText: then shalt thou turn it into money, and bind up the money in thy hand, and shalt go unto the place which Jehovah thy God shall choose:

units.leftText: Then you may spend the money on anything you desire: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink, or anything you wish. You are to feast there in the presence of the LORD your God and rejoice with your household.
units.rightText: and thou shalt bestow the money for whatsoever thy soul desireth, for oxen, or for sheep, or for wine, or for strong drink, or for whatsoever thy soul asketh of thee; and thou shalt eat there before Jehovah thy God, and thou shalt rejoice, thou and thy household.

units.leftText: And do not neglect the Levite within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.
units.rightText: And the Levite that is within thy gates, thou shalt not forsake him; for he hath no portion nor inheritance with thee.

units.leftText: At the end of every three years, bring a tenth of all your produce for that year and lay it up within your gates.
units.rightText: At the end of every three years thou shalt bring forth all the tithe of thine increase in the same year, and shalt lay it up within thy gates:

units.leftText: Then the Levite (because he has no portion or inheritance among you), the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow within your gates may come and eat and be satisfied. And the LORD your God will bless you in all the work of your hands.
units.rightText: and the Levite, because he hath no portion nor inheritance with thee, and the sojourner, and the fatherless, and the widow, that are within thy gates, shall come, and shall eat and be satisfied; that Jehovah thy God may bless thee in all the work of thy hand which thou doest.

units.leftText: At the end of every seven years you must cancel debts.
units.rightText: At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release.

units.leftText: This is the manner of remission: Every creditor shall cancel what he has loaned to his neighbor. He is not to collect anything from his neighbor or brother, because the LORD’s time of release has been proclaimed.
units.rightText: And this is the manner of the release: every creditor shall release that which he hath lent unto his neighbor; he shall not exact it of his neighbor and his brother; because Jehovah’s release hath been proclaimed.

units.leftText: You may collect something from a foreigner, but you must forgive whatever your brother owes you.
units.rightText: Of a foreigner thou mayest exact it: but whatsoever of thine is with thy brother thy hand shall release.

units.leftText: There will be no poor among you, however, because the LORD will surely bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess as an inheritance,
units.rightText: Howbeit there shall be no poor with thee (for Jehovah will surely bless thee in the land which Jehovah thy God giveth thee for an inheritance to possess it),

units.leftText: if only you obey the LORD your God and are careful to follow all these commandments I am giving you today.
units.rightText: if only thou diligently hearken unto the voice of Jehovah thy God, to observe to do all this commandment which I command thee this day.

units.leftText: When the LORD your God blesses you as He has promised, you will lend to many nations but borrow from none; you will rule over many nations but be ruled by none. Generosity in Lending and Giving (Matthew 6:1–4|MAT 6:1-4*)
units.rightText: For Jehovah thy God will bless thee, as he promised thee: and thou shalt lend unto many nations, but thou shalt not borrow; and thou shalt rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over thee.

units.leftText: If there is a poor man among your brothers within any of the gates in the land that the LORD your God is giving you, then you are not to harden your heart or shut your hand from your poor brother.
units.rightText: If there be with thee a poor man, one of thy brethren, within any of thy gates in thy land which Jehovah thy God giveth thee, thou shalt not harden thy heart, nor shut thy hand from thy poor brother;
leftNotes: 15:7 Or make strong or make courageous

units.leftText: Instead, you are to open your hand to him and freely loan him whatever he needs.
units.rightText: but thou shalt surely open thy hand unto him, and shalt surely lend him sufficient for his need in that which he wanteth.

units.leftText: Be careful not to harbor this wicked thought in your heart: “The seventh year, the year of release, is near,” so that you look upon your poor brother begrudgingly and give him nothing. He will cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
units.rightText: Beware that there be not a base thought in thy heart, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand; and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou give him nought; and he cry unto Jehovah against thee, and it be sin unto thee.

units.leftText: Give generously to him, and do not let your heart be grieved when you do so. And because of this the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything to which you put your hand.
units.rightText: Thou shalt surely give him, and thy heart shall not be grieved when thou givest unto him; because that for this thing Jehovah thy God will bless thee in all thy work, and in all that thou puttest thy hand unto.

units.leftText: For there will never cease to be poor in the land; that is why I am commanding you to open wide your hand to your brother and to the poor and needy in your land. Hebrew Servants (Exodus 21:1–11|EXO 21:1-11*)
units.rightText: For the poor will never cease out of the land: therefore I command thee, saying, Thou shalt surely open thy hand unto thy brother, to thy needy, and to thy poor, in thy land.

units.leftText: If a fellow Hebrew, a man or a woman, is sold to you and serves you six years, then in the seventh year you must set him free.
units.rightText: If thy brother, a Hebrew man, or a Hebrew woman, be sold unto thee, and serve thee six years; then in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free from thee.
leftNotes: 15:12 Or sells himself

units.leftText: And when you release him, do not send him away empty-handed.
units.rightText: And when thou lettest him go free from thee, thou shalt not let him go empty:

units.leftText: You are to furnish him liberally from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. You shall give to him as the LORD your God has blessed you.
units.rightText: thou shalt furnish him liberally out of thy flock, and out of thy threshing-floor, and out of thy winepress; as Jehovah thy God hath blessed thee thou shalt give unto him.

units.leftText: Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you; that is why I am giving you this command today.
units.rightText: And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt, and Jehovah thy God redeemed thee: therefore I command thee this thing to-day.

units.leftText: But if your servant says to you, ‘I do not want to leave you,’ because he loves you and your household and is well off with you,
units.rightText: And it shall be, if he say unto thee, I will not go out from thee; because he loveth thee and thy house, because he is well with thee;

units.leftText: then take an awl and pierce it through his ear into the door, and he will become your servant for life. And treat your maidservant the same way.
units.rightText: then thou shalt take an awl, and thrust it through his ear unto the door, and he shall be thy servant for ever. And also unto thy maid-servant thou shalt do likewise.

units.leftText: Do not regard it as a hardship to set your servant free, because his six years of service were worth twice the wages of a hired hand. And the LORD your God will bless you in all you do. Firstborn Animals (Exodus 13:1–16|EXO 13:1-16*)
units.rightText: It shall not seem hard unto thee, when thou lettest him go free from thee; for to the double of the hire of a hireling hath he served thee six years: and Jehovah thy God will bless thee in all that thou doest.

units.leftText: You must set apart to the LORD your God every firstborn male produced by your herds and flocks. You are not to put the firstborn of your oxen to work, nor are you to shear the firstborn of your flock.
units.rightText: All the firstling males that are born of thy herd and of thy flock thou shalt sanctify unto Jehovah thy God: thou shalt do no work with the firstling of thy herd, nor shear the firstling of thy flock.

units.leftText: Each year you and your household are to eat it before the LORD your God in the place the LORD will choose.
units.rightText: Thou shalt eat it before Jehovah thy God year by year in the place which Jehovah shall choose, thou and thy household.

units.leftText: But if an animal has a defect, is lame or blind, or has any serious flaw, you must not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
units.rightText: And if it have any blemish, as if it be lame or blind, any ill blemish whatsoever, thou shalt not sacrifice it unto Jehovah thy God.

units.leftText: Eat it within your gates; both the ceremonially unclean and clean may eat it as they would a gazelle or a deer.
units.rightText: Thou shalt eat it within thy gates: the unclean and the clean shall eat it alike, as the gazelle, and as the hart.

units.leftText: But you must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.
units.rightText: Only thou shalt not eat the blood thereof; thou shalt pour it out upon the ground as water.

units.leftText: Observe the month of Abib and celebrate the Passover to the LORD your God, because in the month of Abib the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
units.rightText: Observe the month of Abib, and keep the passover unto Jehovah thy God; for in the month of Abib Jehovah thy God brought thee forth out of Egypt by night.
leftNotes: 16:1 Abib was the first month of the ancient Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of March and April; twice in this verse.

units.leftText: You are to offer to the LORD your God the Passover sacrifice from the herd or flock in the place the LORD will choose as a dwelling for His Name.
units.rightText: And thou shalt sacrifice the passover unto Jehovah thy God, of the flock and the herd, in the place which Jehovah shall choose, to cause his name to dwell there.

units.leftText: You must not eat leavened bread with it; for seven days you are to eat with it unleavened bread, the bread of affliction, because you left the land of Egypt in haste— so that you may remember for the rest of your life the day you left the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: Thou shalt eat no leavened bread with it; seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread therewith, even the bread of affliction; for thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt in haste: that thou mayest remember the day when thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt all the days of thy life.

units.leftText: No leaven is to be found in all your land for seven days, and none of the meat you sacrifice in the evening of the first day shall remain until morning.
units.rightText: And there shall be no leaven seen with thee in all thy borders seven days; neither shall any of the flesh, which thou sacrificest the first day at even, remain all night until the morning.

units.leftText: You are not to sacrifice the Passover animal in any of the towns that the LORD your God is giving you.
units.rightText: Thou mayest not sacrifice the passover within any of thy gates, which Jehovah thy God giveth thee;

units.leftText: You must only offer the Passover sacrifice at the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for His Name. Do this in the evening as the sun sets, at the same time you departed from Egypt.
units.rightText: but at the place which Jehovah thy God shall choose, to cause his name to dwell in, there thou shalt sacrifice the passover at even, at the going down of the sun, at the season that thou camest forth out of Egypt.

units.leftText: And you shall roast it and eat it in the place the LORD your God will choose, and in the morning you shall return to your tents.
units.rightText: And thou shalt roast and eat it in the place which Jehovah thy God shall choose: and thou shalt turn in the morning, and go unto thy tents.

units.leftText: For six days you must eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day you shall hold a solemn assembly to the LORD your God, and you must not do any work. The Feast of Weeks (Numbers 28:26–31|NUM 28:26-31*)
units.rightText: Six days thou shalt eat unleavened bread; and on the seventh day shall be a solemn assembly to Jehovah thy God; thou shalt do no work therein.

units.leftText: You are to count off seven weeks from the time you first put the sickle to the standing grain.
units.rightText: Seven weeks shalt thou number unto thee: from the time thou beginnest to put the sickle to the standing grain shalt thou begin to number seven weeks.

units.leftText: And you shall celebrate the Feast of Weeks to the LORD your God with a freewill offering that you give in proportion to how the LORD your God has blessed you,
units.rightText: And thou shalt keep the feast of weeks unto Jehovah thy God with a tribute of a freewill-offering of thy hand, which thou shalt give, according as Jehovah thy God blesseth thee:
leftNotes: 16:10 That is, Shavuot; see footnotes for verse 16.

units.leftText: and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God in the place He will choose as a dwelling for His Name — you, your sons and daughters, your menservants and maidservants, and the Levite within your gates, as well as the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widows among you.
units.rightText: and thou shalt rejoice before Jehovah thy God, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter, and thy man-servant, and thy maid-servant, and the Levite that is within thy gates, and the sojourner, and the fatherless, and the widow, that are in the midst of thee, in the place which Jehovah thy God shall choose, to cause his name to dwell there.

units.leftText: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and carefully follow these statutes. The Feast of Tabernacles (Numbers 29:12–40|NUM 29:12-40*)
units.rightText: And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt: and thou shalt observe and do these statutes.

units.leftText: You are to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days after you have gathered the produce of your threshing floor and your winepress.
units.rightText: Thou shalt keep the feast of tabernacles seven days, after that thou hast gathered in from thy threshing-floor and from thy winepress:
leftNotes: 16:13 Or Booths or Shelters; see footnotes for verse 16.

units.leftText: And you shall rejoice in your feast— you, your sons and daughters, your menservants and maidservants, and the Levite, as well as the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widows among you.
units.rightText: and thou shalt rejoice in thy feast, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter, and thy man-servant, and thy maid-servant, and the Levite, and the sojourner, and the fatherless, and the widow, that are within thy gates.

units.leftText: For seven days you shall celebrate a feast to the LORD your God in the place He will choose, because the LORD your God will bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, so that your joy will be complete.
units.rightText: Seven days shalt thou keep a feast unto Jehovah thy God in the place which Jehovah shall choose; because Jehovah thy God will bless thee in all thine increase, and in all the work of thy hands, and thou shalt be altogether joyful.

units.leftText: Three times a year all your men are to appear before the LORD your God in the place He will choose: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles. No one should appear before the LORD empty-handed.
units.rightText: Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before Jehovah thy God in the place which he shall choose: in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles; and they shall not appear before Jehovah empty:
leftNotes: 16:16 That is, the seven-day period after the Passover during which no leaven may be eaten; see Exodus 12:14–20|EXO 12:14-20*.
16:16 That is, Shavuot, the late spring feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; it is also known as the Feast of Harvest(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16*) or the Feast of Pentecost(see Acts 2:1|ACT 2:1*).

16:16 That is, Sukkot, the autumn feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; also translated as the Feast of Booths or the Feast of Shelters and originally called the Feast of Ingathering(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16* and Exodus 34:22).

units.leftText: Everyone must appear with a gift as he is able, according to the blessing the LORD your God has given you. Judges and Justice
units.rightText: every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessing of Jehovah thy God which he hath given thee.

units.leftText: You are to appoint judges and officials for your tribes in every town that the LORD your God is giving you. They are to judge the people with righteous judgment.
units.rightText: Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, which Jehovah thy God giveth thee, according to thy tribes; and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.

units.leftText: Do not deny justice or show partiality. Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not wrest justice: thou shalt not respect persons; neither shalt thou take a bribe; for a bribe doth blind the eyes of the wise, and pervert the words of the righteous.

units.leftText: Pursue justice, and justice alone, so that you may live, and you may possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you. Forbidden Forms of Worship
units.rightText: That which is altogether just shalt thou follow, that thou mayest live, and inherit the land which Jehovah thy God giveth thee.

units.leftText: Do not set up any wooden Asherah pole next to the altar you will build for the LORD your God,
units.rightText: Thou shalt not plant thee an Asherah of any kind of tree beside the altar of Jehovah thy God, which thou shalt make thee.
